analysis.summary_en: This review examines the European experience with RSV prevention following the introduction of nirsevimab, focusing on implementation strategies, effectiveness outcomes, and programme performance. It highlights that real-world studies in Europe have reported significant reductions in RSV hospitalisations and intensive-care admissions after nirsevimab implementation. The review also notes that programme characteristics, such as administration timing, catch-up strategies, and coverage, play a critical role in determining the observed impact. Safety findings remain reassuring, with resistance-associated substitutions not undermining population-level effectiveness. However, the review identifies heterogeneity in programme design and delivery, as well as limitations in cross-strategy comparisons due to timing and selection bias. It concludes that while Europe has demonstrated the potential of universal infant RSV prevention to reduce severe disease burden, standardisation of programme comparisons remains a challenge. The review suggests moving from product advocacy to programme science, emphasizing the need for a primary strategy, rescue indications, and transparent measurement of equity and opportunity costs. The introduction of clesrovimab is noted as an additional preventive option.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 欧洲在两个季节内从针对一小部分高危人群的选择性 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 预防转向能够保护大多数婴儿的基于人群的策略。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 我们的目的是研究 尼塞韦单抗 引入后欧洲在 RSV 预防方面的经验,并确定有关实施、计划绩效、比较评估和剩余证据差距的关键经验教训。检索了 尼塞韦单抗 在欧洲引入后评估 RSV 预防的研究。根据实施策略、有效性结果、医疗保健影响、安全性、阻力和新出现的研究问题绘制证据。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 来自欧洲的真实世界研究一致报告,实施 尼塞韦单抗 后,RSV 住院和重症监护入院人数大幅减少。安全调查结果仍然令人放心;与耐药性相关的替代是可检测到的,但并未损害人群水平的有效性。欧洲的教训并不是一个通用的产品排名:分娩架构、追赶以及产妇 疫苗接种 和出生之间的间隔决定了人口影响。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 计划设计和交付的异质性表明,产品有效性只是影响的决定因素之一:管理时间、追赶策略、覆盖范围、孕产与社区交付以及基线负担的年龄分布等计划特征影响观察到的结果。尽管跨策略比较仍然容易受到时间和选择偏差的影响,但在分娩前充分施用时,母体 RSVpreF 疫苗接种 非常有效。第二季政策需要估算和纪律:有限的剩余效益可以与大量累积的两季效益并存,并且不会反弹。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 下一阶段应从产品宣传转向项目科学:针对大多数婴儿的主要策略、明确的救援适应症、关联的免疫结果-基因组监测、共同估计值以及公平和机会成本的透明衡量。最近推出的 clesrovimab 进一步扩大了预防选择。

title: Respiratory Virus Activity — United States, July 2025–June 2026
abstract: Respiratory viral illnesses are common and can lead to severe outcomes, including hospitalization and death. trends in respiratory virus activity during July 2025-June 2026 were analyzed using data from six complementary public health surveillance systems. Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) activity occurred unusually late in most U.S. SARS-CoV-2 circulated nationally with typical bimodal peaks that occurred in August 2025 and January 2026. Annual RSV-associated hospitalization rates (number of hospitalizations per 100,000 persons) were highest among infants aged <12 months (790.2; 95% CI = 757.9-825.3), followed by children aged 12-23 months (611.9; 95% CI = 586.3-639.8) and adults aged ≥75 years (352.1; 95% CI = 309.9-407.7). Annual RSV rates overall and by age group did not exceed those observed during 2022-2025. COVID-19-associated hospitalization rates were highest among adults aged ≥75 years (361.2), infants aged <6 months (173.3), and adults aged 65-74 years (111.4). Newly established 2025-2026 national pediatric mortality surveillance provisionally identified 34 RSV-associated pediatric deaths from 35 reporting jurisdictions and 31 COVID-19-associated pediatric deaths from 43 reporting jurisdictions. RSV sequencing did not identify variant substitutions associated with reduced susceptibility to the available RSV monoclonal antibodies for infants. Most SARS-CoV-2 lineages were JN.1 descendants, but detections of BA.3.2, a highly divergent SARS-CoV-2 variant, increased. Circulation of other respiratory viruses followed usual historical patterns. Staying current with recommended RSV and COVID-19 vaccinations reduces the risk for severe illness and disease caused by these viruses.
authors: Coronavirus and Other Respiratory Viruses Division Laboratory Genomic Surveillance Group

title: Harnessing mucosal and systemic immunity against respiratory viruses: vaccine platforms, delivery strategies, and adjuvants
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Long-lasting immunity against respiratory viruses, including influenza, COVID-19, and respiratory syncytial virus, remains a challenge. Effective vaccines and vaccination strategies that confer durable protection against these viruses require the induction of both systemic and mucosal immunity. AREA COVERED: This review covers the latest trends in respiratory viral vaccine platforms, including modified virus-like particles and mRNA-based vaccines, as well as adjuvants, and new vaccination strategies that induce systemic and mucosal immunity and generate lung-resident memory cells. A better understanding of innate immune responses to vaccination is critical for improving vaccine efficacy and safety and for identifying early predictive correlates. EXPERT OPINION: This article outlines recent advances and approaches to developing next-generation respiratory viral vaccines and new vaccination strategies to induce systemic and mucosal immunity. It also discusses the gap between preclinical and clinical outcomes of mucosal vaccination.

Effective vaccines and vaccination strategies that confer durable protection against these viruses require the induction of both systemic and mucosal immunity. AREA COVERED: This review covers the latest trends in respiratory viral vaccine platforms, including modified virus-like particles and mRNA-based vaccines, as well as adjuvants, and new vaccination strategies that induce systemic and mucosal immunity and generate lung-resident memory cells. A better understanding of innate immune responses to vaccination is critical for improving vaccine efficacy and safety and for identifying early predictive correlates. EXPERT OPINION: This article outlines recent advances and approaches to developing next-generation respiratory viral vaccines and new vaccination strategies to induce systemic and mucosal immunity. It also discusses the gap between preclinical and clinical outcomes of mucosal vaccination.

title: Multi-model forecasting of respiratory disease activity in Germany during the 2024–2025 season
abstract: Respiratory diseases cause considerable morbidity in autumn and winter and are a priority in public health monitoring. In Germany, they are subject to a number of surveillance systems, including both pathogen-specific and syndromic indicators. In this paper we present a collaborative multi-target and multi-model real-time forecasting system rolled out during the 2024/25 season, and discuss differences to earlier efforts carried out during the COVID-19 pandemic. We focus on general practitioner consultations for acute respiratory infections (ARI) and hospitalizations for severe acute respiratory infections (SARI), where a total of eight models were run to generate nowcasts and forecasts. In addition, we consider confirmed cases of seasonal influenza and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) where one forecasting model each was available. As all indicators were subject to retrospective revisions, forecasting models were combined with a nowcasting step. For the SARI and ARI indicators, we combined the available models into an ensemble and conducted detailed quantitative evaluations. Nowcasts overall showed convincing performance, even though for some models Christmas break effects led to an upward bias in early January. Forecasts were overall well-calibrated and most models outperformed simple benchmark models. When taking into account age-stratified targets, most observed performance differences to a persistence baseline were statistically significant. Anticipating the peak timing and magnitude, however, proved to be challenging, with many models predicting too flat curves with a too early turnaround (e.g., in late January rather than mid-February for SARI). The combined ensemble forecast was among the best-performing approaches, but unlike in previous related projects did not consistently outperform individual models. We conclude by discussing learnings on the organization of collaborative forecasting projects in post-COVID-19 times.

Anticipating the peak timing and magnitude, however, proved to be challenging, with many models predicting too flat curves with a too early turnaround (e.g., in late January rather than mid-February for SARI). title: Developing a syndromic case definition for timely surveillance of severe acute respiratory infections (SARI) based on financial claim codes in the Netherlands
abstract: INTRODUCTION: To improve pandemic preparedness, a sustainable and timely surveillance system for severe acute respiratory infections (SARI) is crucial. We developed and evaluated a proxy for syndromic SARI-surveillance using financial claim codes (DTC-codes). METHODS: With data from 2016-2020 we compared DTC-codes with primary discharge diagnosis classified by ICD-10 codes (J0-J22, U07) as comparative benchmark for SARI, distinguishing between paediatric and adult populations, and pre- and during COVID-19-pandemic periods. To establish DTC-based proxies for SARI, accuracy metrics of individual and combinations of DTC-codes, and temporal trends were assessed. We retrospectively assessed its ability to detect COVID-19 epidemic patterns and its relationship with outcomes of existing respiratory surveillance systems. RESULTS: For adults, DTC-codes for pneumonia and unspecified respiratory and viral infections served as proxy for SARI. In the paediatric population, codes for laryngitis subglottica, RSV bronchiolitis and respiratory tract infection were used. While trends in DTC-based SARI proxies correlate with trends in ICD-10-coded SARI, the accuracy relative to this benchmark was moderate. The adult DTC-based SARI proxy reflected peaks in COVID-19 hospitalisations during the pandemic and aligned with influenza and RSV laboratory detections in the pre-pandemic period. The paediatric DTC-based SARI proxy aligned with RSV laboratory detections. CONCLUSION: We established DTC-based proxies for syndromic SARI-surveillance that appeared suitable to monitor SARI-trends. However, on the patient level the accuracy for ICD-10-coded SARI appeared moderate. Accuracy of the DTC-based SARI proxy and its ability to detect relevant epidemic signals, should be assessed prospectively with real-time data.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to develop a syndromic case definition for timely surveillance of severe acute respiratory infections (SARI) using financial claim codes (DTC-codes) in the Netherlands. The researchers compared DTC-codes with ICD-10 codes (J0-J22, U07) as a benchmark for SARI, analyzing both adult and pediatric populations across pre- and during the COVID-19 pandemic periods. For adults, DTC-codes for pneumonia and unspecified respiratory and viral infections were identified as proxies for SARI, while in the pediatric population, codes for laryngitis subglottica, RSV bronchiolitis, and respiratory tract infection were used. The results showed that the DTC-based proxies correlated with ICD-10-coded SARI trends, with moderate accuracy. The adult proxy reflected peaks in COVID-19 hospitalizations and aligned with influenza and RSV laboratory detections, while the pediatric proxy aligned with RSV laboratory detections. The authors concluded that DTC-based proxies for SARI surveillance appear suitable for monitoring trends, but their accuracy and ability to detect epidemic signals should be assessed prospectively with real-time data. The study's findings may inform the development of surveillance systems for SARI, particularly in the context of respiratory viruses like RSV, but the evidence is limited to retrospective analysis and moderate accuracy.

title_zh: 根据荷兰的财务索赔代码,为严重急性呼吸道感染 (SARI) 的及时 监测 制定综合征病例定义
source_body_en: INTRODUCTION: To improve pandemic preparedness, a sustainable and timely surveillance system for severe acute respiratory infections (SARI) is crucial. We developed and evaluated a proxy for syndromic SARI-surveillance using financial claim codes (DTC-codes). METHODS: With data from 2016-2020 we compared DTC-codes with primary discharge diagnosis classified by ICD-10 codes (J0-J22, U07) as comparative benchmark for SARI, distinguishing between paediatric and adult populations, and pre- and during COVID-19-pandemic periods. To establish DTC-based proxies for SARI, accuracy metrics of individual and combinations of DTC-codes, and temporal trends were assessed. We retrospectively assessed its ability to detect COVID-19 epidemic patterns and its relationship with outcomes of existing respiratory surveillance systems. RESULTS: For adults, DTC-codes for pneumonia and unspecified respiratory and viral infections served as proxy for SARI. In the paediatric population, codes for laryngitis subglottica, RSV bronchiolitis and respiratory tract infection were used. While trends in DTC-based SARI proxies correlate with trends in ICD-10-coded SARI, the accuracy relative to this benchmark was moderate. The adult DTC-based SARI proxy reflected peaks in COVID-19 hospitalisations during the pandemic and aligned with influenza and RSV laboratory detections in the pre-pandemic period. The paediatric DTC-based SARI proxy aligned with RSV laboratory detections. CONCLUSION: We established DTC-based proxies for syndromic SARI-surveillance that appeared suitable to monitor SARI-trends. However, on the patient level the accuracy for ICD-10-coded SARI appeared moderate. Accuracy of the DTC-based SARI proxy and its ability to detect relevant epidemic signals, should be assessed prospectively with real-time data.
abstract_zh: 简介:为了改善大流行的防范,针对严重急性呼吸道感染 (SARI) 的可持续且及时的 监测 系统至关重要。我们使用财务索赔代码(DTC 代码)开发并评估了综合症 SARI-监测 的代理。方法:根据 2016-2020 年的数据,我们将 DTC 代码与按 ICD-10 代码(J0-J22、U07)分类的初次出院 诊断 进行比较,作为 SARI 的比较基准,区分儿童和成人人群以及 COVID-19 大流行之前和期间。为了建立基于 DTC 的 SARI 代理,评估了 DTC 代码的个体和组合的准确性指标以及时间趋势。我们回顾性评估了其检测 COVID-19 流行模式的能力及其与现有呼吸 监测 系统结果的关系。结果:对于成年人来说,肺炎和未明确的呼吸道和病毒感染的 DTC 代码可以作为 SARI 的代表。在儿科人群中,使用了声门下喉炎、RSV 毛细支气管炎 和呼吸道感染的代码。虽然基于 DTC 的 SARI 代理的趋势与 ICD-10 编码的 SARI 的趋势相关,但相对于该基准的准确性适中。基于成人 DTC 的 SARI 指标反映了大流行期间 COVID-19 住院治疗的高峰,并与大流行前时期的流感和 RSV 实验室检测结果一致。基于儿科 DTC 的 SARI 代理与 RSV 实验室检测一致。结论:我们为综合症 SARI-监测 建立了基于 DTC 的代理,该代理似乎适合监测 SARI 趋势。然而,在患者层面,ICD-10 编码的 SARI 的准确性似乎中等。应使用实时数据前瞻性评估基于 DTC 的 SARI 代理的准确性及其检测相关流行病信号的能力。

title: RSV and all-cause lower respiratory infection burden among infants residing in remote British Columbia: Retrospective population-based birth cohort study
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To determine the population-based incidence of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection-related hospitalization in infancy by community remoteness. METHODS: Retrospective cohort study of live births within an integrated health jurisdiction in British Columbia (BC, Canada) from April 2013 to March 2024, followed for 1 year, using routinely collected health administrative data. Main outcomes were hospitalizations for all-cause and RSV-associated lower respiratory tract infection (LRTI). Secondary outcomes were tertiary pediatric intensive care unit (PICU) admissions, length of stay, and air transport. Main exposures were community remoteness and social determinants of health. Incidence rate ratios (IRRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were estimated with Poisson generalized estimating equations accounting for clustering by community, with and without additional adjustment for sex, prematurity, and chronic conditions. RESULTS: Among 472,623 infants, those living in remote communities (n = 3636) had higher hospitalization risk for all-cause (IRR 2.91, 95% CI 2.24-3.79) and RSV-LRTIs (IRR 1.60, 95% CI 1.17-2.19) compared to metropolitan areas. Length of stay and PICU admission rates were similar by region. Almost half (48.8%) of children from remote areas hospitalized for RSV-LRTIs required air evacuation. Infants from remote communities remained at higher risk for all-cause (aIRR 2.84, 95% CI 2.22-3.63) and RSV-LRTI (aIRR 1.56, 95% CI 1.15-2.12) hospitalizations after adjusting for covariates. CONCLUSION: Infants in remote communities experienced a disproportionately high burden of RSV and all-cause LRTI hospitalization that is not fully explained by measured clinical or social determinants of health. These findings underscore the need for region-specific approaches and equitable implementation of prevention programs as jurisdictions move toward universal RSV immunization.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to assess the population-based incidence of RSV infection-related hospitalizations in infants, focusing on disparities linked to community remoteness.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective cohort study was conducted on live births in British Columbia, Canada, from April 2013 to March 2024, with follow-up for one year. The study included 472,623 infants, with a subset (n = 3636) residing in remote communities.
analysis.methods: The study used routinely collected health administrative data to evaluate hospitalizations for all-cause and RSV-associated lower respiratory tract infections (LRTIs), along with secondary outcomes such as tertiary PICU admissions, length of stay, and air transport. Incidence rate ratios (IRRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were estimated using Poisson generalized estimating equations, accounting for clustering by community and adjusting for sex, prematurity, and chronic conditions.
analysis.main_results: Infants from remote communities had higher hospitalization risks for all-cause LRTIs (IRR 2.91, 95% CI 2.24-3.79) and RSV-LRTIs (IRR 1.60, 95% CI 1.17-2.19) compared to those in metropolitan areas. After adjusting for covariates, the risk remained elevated for all-cause LRTIs (aIRR 2.84, 95% CI 2.22-3.63) and RSV-LRTIs (aIRR 1.56, 95% CI 1.15-2.12).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that the higher hospitalization rates in remote communities for RSV and all-cause LRTIs are not fully explained by the measured clinical or social determinants of health, highlighting a novel finding of geographic disparities in disease burden.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest the need for region-specific prevention strategies and equitable implementation of RSV immunization programs to address the disproportionately high burden of RSV and all-cause LRTI hospitalizations in remote areas.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on routinely collected administrative data, which may have missing or inaccurate information. However, the evidence is strong, with adjusted incidence rate ratios providing a clear indication of the increased risk in remote communities.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the incidence of RSV infection-related hospitalizations among infants in remote versus metropolitan communities in British Columbia. Using a retrospective cohort design, it found that infants in remote areas had significantly higher risks of hospitalization for both all-cause and RSV-associated lower respiratory tract infections. The results remained consistent even after adjusting for factors such as sex, prematurity, and chronic conditions. The authors concluded that the increased burden is not fully explained by measured determinants, emphasizing the need for targeted prevention strategies. The study's reliance on administrative data introduces potential limitations, but the findings are robust and have important implications for public health policy in remote regions.

title_zh: 居住在不列颠哥伦比亚省偏远地区的婴儿的 RSV 和全因下呼吸道感染负担:基于人群的出生回顾性 队列研究 研究
source_body_en: OBJECTIVE: To determine the population-based incidence of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection-related hospitalization in infancy by community remoteness. METHODS: Retrospective cohort study of live births within an integrated health jurisdiction in British Columbia (BC, Canada) from April 2013 to March 2024, followed for 1 year, using routinely collected health administrative data. Main outcomes were hospitalizations for all-cause and RSV-associated lower respiratory tract infection (LRTI). Secondary outcomes were tertiary pediatric intensive care unit (PICU) admissions, length of stay, and air transport. Main exposures were community remoteness and social determinants of health. Incidence rate ratios (IRRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were estimated with Poisson generalized estimating equations accounting for clustering by community, with and without additional adjustment for sex, prematurity, and chronic conditions. RESULTS: Among 472,623 infants, those living in remote communities (n = 3636) had higher hospitalization risk for all-cause (IRR 2.91, 95% CI 2.24-3.79) and RSV-LRTIs (IRR 1.60, 95% CI 1.17-2.19) compared to metropolitan areas. Length of stay and PICU admission rates were similar by region. Almost half (48.8%) of children from remote areas hospitalized for RSV-LRTIs required air evacuation. Infants from remote communities remained at higher risk for all-cause (aIRR 2.84, 95% CI 2.22-3.63) and RSV-LRTI (aIRR 1.56, 95% CI 1.15-2.12) hospitalizations after adjusting for covariates. CONCLUSION: Infants in remote communities experienced a disproportionately high burden of RSV and all-cause LRTI hospitalization that is not fully explained by measured clinical or social determinants of health. These findings underscore the need for region-specific approaches and equitable implementation of prevention programs as jurisdictions move toward universal RSV immunization.

title: EFFECTIVENESS OF MATERNAL RSV VACCINATION IN PREVENTING RSV-RELATED PRIMARY CARE ATTENDANCE IN INFANTS: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW AND META-ANALYSIS
abstract: Background: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) disease places a substantial burden on primary care. Maternal RSV vaccination reduces severe RSV disease and hospitalisation among infants; however, its effects on primary care, where most RSV infections are managed, remain poorly understood. We investigated the effect of maternal RSV vaccination on RSV-related primary care attendance. Methods: This systematic review and meta-analysis was prospectively registered with PROSPERO (CRD420251169070). MEDLINE, Embase, MIDIRS, CINAHL, Cochrane CENTRAL and Scopus were searched for studies published between January 2000 and January 2026. Eligible studies included pregnant women receiving an RSV vaccine, infants born to vaccinated mothers, a placebo or unvaccinated comparator, and RSV-related infant outcomes including medically attended illness and/or hospitalisation. Random-effects meta-analyses were undertaken. As no studies specifically reported primary care attendance, medically attended RSV lower respiratory tract infection (RSV-LRTI) was used as a proxy. Results: Four randomised controlled trials involving 17,289 infants born to mothers receiving RSV vaccination or placebo met inclusion criteria. Maternal vaccination reduced medically attended RSV-LRTI at 90 days (OR 0.51, 95% CI 0.38–0.69; p<0.001), with protection persisting to 180 days (OR 0.53, 95% CI 0.35–0.80; p<0.003). RSV-LRTI hospitalisation was also reduced (OR 0.56, 95% CI 0.42–0.76; p<0.001). Two studies had low risk of bias and two had some concerns. Conclusions: Maternal RSV vaccination reduces medically attended RSV-LRTI and hospitalisation during the first six months of life, potentially reducing primary care burden. Real-world studies are needed to confirm its impact on primary care attendance. Key messages: · Maternal RSV vaccination reduces severe RSV disease and hospitalisation in infants, but its impact in primary care, where much RSV illness is managed, is poorly understood. · Maternal RSV vaccination reduces medically attended RSV-LRTI at 90 and 180 days; however, no studies reported primary care attendance specifically, requiring medically attended RSV-LRTI to be used as a proxy. · The lack of primary care-specific evidence highlights the need for real-world studies assessing the impact of maternal RSV vaccination on primary care consultations and referrals to secondary care.

abstract: Longitudinal sequencing can reveal fine-grained pathogen evolution during acute and chronic infections and inform public health responses. However, integrating ordered pathogen genomic data into a coherent evolutionary and clinical framework can be tedious and error-prone. We present vartracker, an open-source tool for longitudinal pathogen variant analysis and visualization. Given an ordered sample manifest, vartracker supports three entry points: raw sequence reads, reference-aligned BAM files, or user-supplied variant-call format (VCF) files and coverage inputs. Raw-read and BAM inputs are processed through an integrated Snakemake workflow, whereas VCF mode starts from precomputed files. Variants are normalized and annotated relative to a reference genome, tracked across timepoints, and classified as original or newly emerging and as transient or persistent. Inferred amino acid changes are reported, and for SARS-CoV-2 analyses, relevant published literature for key mutations can be automatically linked through a functional database. vartracker outputs a schema-documented results table, provenance metadata for reproducibility, publication-quality static figures, and an interactive heatmap for data exploration. Although packaged with SARS-CoV-2 reference assets and initially developed for SARS-CoV-2 datasets, vartracker is pathogen-agnostic when appropriate reference data are supplied. We demonstrate its utility using SARS-CoV-2 and respiratory syncytial virus A (RSV-A) datasets. vartracker is freely available through GitHub, PyPI, and Bioconda.

title: Diverse lung challenges elicit a conserved monocyte-to-macrophage differentiation blueprint
abstract: Alveolar macrophages (AMs) form a first line of defense to lung insults. These insults often lead to replacement of fetal-derived tissue-resident AMs (fAMs) by monocyte-derived AMs (mono-AMs) with different functionality, which impacts lung immunity during future lung challenges. However, whether these alterations are conserved or insult specific is not well understood. Here we show that respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection remodels the AM compartment long term. We perform comparative analyses of fAMs and mono-AMs after RSV infection, influenza A virus infection or clodronate liposome administration and identify a crucial tissue integration checkpoint of CD11b + mono-AMs that involves acquisition of proliferative capacity and requires EGR2-mediated transcriptional rewiring. Mono-AMs elicited by RSV, influenza A virus or clodronate liposomes have a hardwired ontogeny-dependent stereotypical profile of transcription, proliferation, metabolism and enhanced immunoreactivity despite a substantially different inflammatory environment during differentiation; accordingly, mono-AMs elicited by sterile or infectious insult protect from subsequent Streptococcus pneumoniae infection. By contrast, fAMs display context-dependent transcriptional alterations. Our findings highlight that long-term changes in the AM compartment show origin-dependent phenotypic divergence and that mono-AM integration follows a hardwired trajectory fine-tuned by environmental factors.

However, whether these alterations are conserved or insult specific is not well understood. Here we show that respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection remodels the AM compartment long term. We perform comparative analyses of fAMs and mono-AMs after RSV infection, influenza A virus infection or clodronate liposome administration and identify a crucial tissue integration checkpoint of CD11b + mono-AMs that involves acquisition of proliferative capacity and requires EGR2-mediated transcriptional rewiring. Mono-AMs elicited by RSV, influenza A virus or clodronate liposomes have a hardwired ontogeny-dependent stereotypical profile of transcription, proliferation, metabolism and enhanced immunoreactivity despite a substantially different inflammatory environment during differentiation; accordingly, mono-AMs elicited by sterile or infectious insult protect from subsequent Streptococcus pneumoniae infection. By contrast, fAMs display context-dependent transcriptional alterations. Our findings highlight that long-term changes in the AM compartment show origin-dependent phenotypic divergence and that mono-AM integration follows a hardwired trajectory fine-tuned by environmental factors.

title: Lipid Nanoparticle–mRNA Vaccines for Infectious Diseases: Making a Potent Platform Predictable
abstract: Lipid nanoparticle (LNP)–mRNA vaccines compressed the path from pathogen sequence to licensed product into less than a year and are now approved for three viral diseases (COVID-19, respiratory syncytial virus and seasonal influenza), with more than twenty indications in clinical development. The platform’s potency is no longer in doubt; its predictability is. We argue that progress is now limited by three interfaces that are engineered largely independently: the lipid–RNA interface, which sets encapsulation, internal structure and storage stability; the particle–cell interface, which sets tropism and the efficiency of endosomal escape; and the particle–immune interface, which sets the balance between adjuvanticity and reactogenicity. Quantitative design rules exist for the first interface, remain empirical for the second, and are almost absent for the third, which is why formulation development still proceeds by screening rather than by calculation. We review the molecular design of the mRNA payload and structural antigen selection; the chemistry, manufacture and intracellular trafficking of LNPs; the immunological chain that links innate activation and dendritic-cell cross-presentation to germinal-centre output; and the clinical evidence across COVID-19, respiratory syncytial virus, influenza, cytomegalovirus, HIV, personalised cancer vaccines and other targets. We conclude by identifying the measurements, pharmacopoeial quality attributes and design rules that would make the next generation of LNP–mRNA vaccines predictable rather than empirical.

title_original: Lipid Nanoparticle–mRNA Vaccines for Infectious Diseases: Making a Potent Platform Predictable

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on lipid nanoparticle (LNP)–mRNA vaccines for respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), including their development, molecular design, and clinical applications. The central question is how to make these vaccines predictable rather than empirical, particularly in the context of RSV and related viral diseases.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a comprehensive analysis of the molecular design of mRNA payloads, structural antigen selection, LNP chemistry and manufacturing, intracellular trafficking, immunological mechanisms, and clinical evidence across various viral targets, including RSV. The review method involves synthesizing findings from multiple studies and highlighting the empirical nature of formulation development.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that the platform’s potency is established, but its predictability remains a challenge. It identifies the need for measurements, pharmacopoeial quality attributes, and design rules to make the next generation of LNP–mRNA vaccines predictable rather than empirical.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review highlights that quantitative design rules exist for the lipid–RNA interface, but remain empirical for the particle–cell interface and almost absent for the particle–immune interface. This lack of predictability in the latter two interfaces is a key evidence gap.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review suggests that future research should focus on developing quantitative design rules for the particle–cell and particle–immune interfaces to improve the predictability and efficiency of LNP–mRNA vaccines for RSV and other targets.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the development and application of lipid nanoparticle (LNP)–mRNA vaccines for respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), emphasizing their rapid deployment and current approval status for several viral diseases. It identifies the platform’s established potency but highlights the lack of predictability in its formulation. The review argues that progress is constrained by three interfaces—lipid–RNA, particle–cell, and particle–immune—that are engineered independently. While quantitative rules exist for the first interface, the second remains empirical, and the third is almost absent, leading to a reliance on screening rather than calculation. The authors conclude that defining measurements, quality attributes, and design rules would enhance the predictability of future LNP–mRNA vaccines. They also suggest that research should prioritize these interfaces to improve vaccine development and application.

analysis_en.scope_and_question: The review focuses on lipid nanoparticle (LNP)–mRNA vaccines for respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), including their development, molecular design, and clinical applications. analysis_en.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a comprehensive analysis of the molecular design of mRNA payloads, structural antigen selection, LNP chemistry and manufacturing, intracellular trafficking, immunological mechanisms, and clinical evidence across various viral targets, including RSV. analysis_en.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that the platform’s potency is established, but its predictability remains a challenge. title_zh: 用于传染病的脂质纳米颗粒 – mRNA 疫苗:打造可预测的有效平台
source_body_en: Lipid nanoparticle (LNP)–mRNA vaccines compressed the path from pathogen sequence to licensed product into less than a year and are now approved for three viral diseases (COVID-19, respiratory syncytial virus and seasonal influenza), with more than twenty indications in clinical development. The platform’s potency is no longer in doubt; its predictability is. We argue that progress is now limited by three interfaces that are engineered largely independently: the lipid–RNA interface, which sets encapsulation, internal structure and storage stability; the particle–cell interface, which sets tropism and the efficiency of endosomal escape; and the particle–immune interface, which sets the balance between adjuvanticity and reactogenicity. Quantitative design rules exist for the first interface, remain empirical for the second, and are almost absent for the third, which is why formulation development still proceeds by screening rather than by calculation. We review the molecular design of the mRNA payload and structural antigen selection; the chemistry, manufacture and intracellular trafficking of LNPs; the immunological chain that links innate activation and dendritic-cell cross-presentation to germinal-centre output; and the clinical evidence across COVID-19, respiratory syncytial virus, influenza, cytomegalovirus, HIV, personalised cancer vaccines and other targets. We conclude by identifying the measurements, pharmacopoeial quality attributes and design rules that would make the next generation of LNP–mRNA vaccines predictable rather than empirical.

title: Aligned Evidence, Aligned Guidance: 2026-2027 Respiratory Virus Immunization Recommendations from The AAFP, AAP, ACOG, AND IDSA.
abstract: Disruption of the federal vaccine advisory process prompted a coordinated, society-led approach to respiratory virus immunization guidance for the 2026-2027 season. The Vaccine Integrity Project (VIP) at the University of Minnesota Center for Infectious Disease Research and Policy, in collaboration with the American Medical Association and with coordination support from the Council of Medical Specialty Societies, completed systematic reviews of influenza, COVID-19, and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) immunization. Across 299 studies, the reviews confirmed protection against hospitalization and death and identified no new safety concerns in comparative studies. On September 2, 2026, the American Academy of Family Physicians (AAFP), American Academy of Pediatrics, American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists, and Infectious Diseases Society of America issued aligned recommendations informed by this evidence. This report explains the shared evidence base, summarizes recommendations by age and population, describes the AAFP review and adoption process, and directs primary care clinicians to implementation and patient resources.

analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 证据基础没有报告任何异质性或相互矛盾的发现。然而,审查并未在比较研究中发现任何新的安全问题,证据也没有报告任何未解决的机制或具体的证据差距。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 初级保健临床医生负责实施和患者资源。该报告解释了共享证据基础,总结了按年龄和人口划分的建议,并描述了 AAFP 审查和采用过程。

title: Validation of Centers for Disease Control and Prevention National Wastewater Surveillance System’s Wastewater Viral Activity Level for Respiratory Viruses, 2025 –2026 Respiratory Season
abstract: Abstract Background The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) developed the Wastewater Viral Activity Level metric (WVAL) for SARS-CoV-2 in 2023 to meet the need for a public metric that aggregates wastewater viral RNA concentration data to provide jurisdictional, regional, and national surveillance system estimates for the United States. The WVAL was expanded in August 2024 to include virus-specific metrics for influenza A and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV). This paper describes results the 2025 validation of the updated WVAL methodology. Methods During validation conducted from March through July 2025, candidate WVAL methods were evaluated using wastewater surveillance data collected through March 22, 2025, from SARS-CoV-2, influenza A, and RSV sampling sites. Evaluated components included the baseline calculation and stabilization period, the frequency of baseline and standard deviation updates, the sample look-back period used to calculate the baseline, and the cut points used to assign WVAL categories. Results Data included 4,447 SARS-CoV-2, 1,592 influenza A, and 1,454 RSV data submitter level sampling sites. A z-score threshold of 4 was selected for outlier removal, and non-normalized wastewater concentrations with a 24-month look-back period were selected for baseline and standard deviation calculations across pathogens. Baseline and standard deviation updates were scheduled for April 1 and October 1 for SARS-CoV-2 and August 1 for influenza A and RSV. An eight-week stabilization period was selected. Median-of-medians aggregation was selected for regional and national estimates, and pathogen-specific cut-points were selected to align WVAL categories with clinical surveillance data. National WVALs were moderately to strongly correlated with emergency department surveillance data for SARS-CoV-2 (Kendall’s tau = 0.78), influenza A (0.81), and RSV (0.74). Conclusions Annual validation supported updates to the WVAL methodology that reduced extreme values, improved comparability across pathogens and geographic levels, and maintained alignment with clinical surveillance. The updated methods provide a more consistent framework for public wastewater surveillance of SARS-CoV-2, influenza A, and RSV.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to validate the updated Wastewater Viral Activity Level (WVAL) methodology for respiratory viruses, including respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), to improve public health surveillance in the United States. The need arose from the CDC's development of the WVAL metric for SARS-CoV-2 in 2023, which highlighted the importance of a standardized approach for viral RNA concentration data aggregation.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted from March through July 2025, evaluating the WVAL methodology using wastewater surveillance data collected through March 22, 2025, from SARS-CoV-2, influenza A, and RSV sampling sites. The population included wastewater data from multiple sampling sites across the United States.
analysis.methods: The validation process involved assessing components such as baseline calculation and stabilization period, frequency of baseline and standard deviation updates, sample look-back period for baseline calculations, and cut points for assigning WVAL categories. A z-score threshold of 4 was selected for outlier removal, and non-normalized wastewater concentrations with a 24-month look-back period were used for baseline and standard deviation calculations across pathogens.
analysis.main_results: The study included data from 4,447 SARS-CoV-2, 1,592 influenza A, and 1,454 RSV data submitter level sampling sites. The methodology was updated to include virus-specific metrics for influenza A and RSV, expanding the WVAL system beyond its initial focus on SARS-CoV-2.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as supporting the updated WVAL methodology, which reduced extreme values, improved comparability across pathogens and geographic levels, and maintained alignment with clinical surveillance data. The novelty lies in the expansion of the WVAL system to include RSV and influenza A.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings provide a more consistent framework for public wastewater surveillance of SARS-CoV-2, influenza A, and RSV, which can inform public health decisions and enhance the accuracy of viral activity monitoring.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to abstract-only evidence, and the methodology was validated using data up to March 22, 2025. The evidence supports a moderate to high confidence in the updated WVAL methodology for respiratory viruses.

analysis.summary_en: This study validates the updated Wastewater Viral Activity Level (WVAL) methodology for respiratory viruses, including respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), developed by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). The WVAL was initially created for SARS-CoV-2 in 2023 and expanded in 2024 to include influenza A and RSV. The validation, conducted from March to July 2025, evaluated components such as baseline calculation, stabilization period, and cut points for assigning WVAL categories. The methodology incorporated a z-score threshold of 4 for outlier removal and used non-normalized wastewater concentrations with a 24-month look-back period. The study included data from 4,447 SARS-CoV-2, 1,592 influenza A, and 1,454 RSV sampling sites. The results indicated that the updated WVAL system provides a more consistent framework for public health surveillance, aligning with clinical data and improving comparability across pathogens. The authors concluded that the methodology effectively reduces extreme values and maintains alignment with clinical surveillance, offering a valuable tool for monitoring viral activity in wastewater. The evidence is abstract-only, and the findings are supported with moderate to high confidence.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在验证更新后的呼吸道病毒废水病毒活性水平 (WVAL) 方法,包括 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV),以改善美国的公共卫生 呼吸道合胞病毒。这一需求源自 CDC 于 2023 年开发的 SARS-CoV-2 WVAL 指标,该指标强调了病毒 RNA 浓度数据聚合标准化方法的重要性。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究于 2025 年 3 月至 7 月期间进行,使用截至 2025 年 3 月 22 日从 SARS-CoV-2、甲型流感和 RSV 采样点收集的废水 监测 数据评估了 WVAL 方法。总体数据包括来自美国多个采样点的废水数据。
elements_zh.methods: 验证过程涉及评估基线计算和稳定期、基线和标准差更新频率、基线计算的样本回顾期以及分配 WVAL 类别的切点等组件。选择 z 分数阈值 4 来去除异常值,并使用具有 24 个月回顾期的非标准化废水浓度来计算病原体的基线和标准偏差。
elements_zh.main_results: 该研究包括来自 4,447 个 SARS-CoV-2、1,592 个甲型流感和 1,454 个 RSV 数据提交者级别采样点的数据。该方法已更新,包括甲型流感和 RSV 的病毒特异性指标,从而将 WVAL 系统扩展到最初关注的 SARS-CoV-2 之外。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为支持更新的 WVAL 方法,该方法减少了极值,提高了病原体和地理水平之间的可比性,并与临床 监测 数据保持一致。新颖之处在于 WVAL 系统的扩展,包括 RSV 和甲型流感。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果为 SARS-CoV-2、甲型流感和 RSV 的公共废水 监测 提供了更加一致的框架,可以为公共卫生决策提供信息并提高病毒活动监测的准确性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于摘要证据,并且使用截至 2025 年 3 月 22 日的数据验证了该方法。这些证据支持更新的呼吸道病毒 WVAL 方法具有中等到高可信度。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在验证更新后的呼吸道病毒废水病毒活性水平 (WVAL) 方法,包括 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV),以改善美国的公共卫生 呼吸道合胞病毒。这一需求源自 CDC 于 2023 年开发的 SARS-CoV-2 WVAL 指标,该指标强调了病毒 RNA 浓度数据聚合标准化方法的重要性。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究于 2025 年 3 月至 7 月期间进行,使用截至 2025 年 3 月 22 日从 SARS-CoV-2、甲型流感和 RSV 采样点收集的废水 监测 数据评估了 WVAL 方法。总体数据包括来自美国多个采样点的废水数据。
analysis_zh.methods: 验证过程涉及评估基线计算和稳定期、基线和标准差更新频率、基线计算的样本回顾期以及分配 WVAL 类别的切点等组件。选择 z 分数阈值 4 来去除异常值,并使用具有 24 个月回顾期的非标准化废水浓度来计算病原体的基线和标准偏差。
analysis_zh.main_results: 该研究包括来自 4,447 个 SARS-CoV-2、1,592 个甲型流感和 1,454 个 RSV 数据提交者级别采样点的数据。该方法已更新,包括甲型流感和 RSV 的病毒特异性指标,从而将 WVAL 系统扩展到最初关注的 SARS-CoV-2 之外。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为支持更新的 WVAL 方法,该方法减少了极值,提高了病原体和地理水平之间的可比性,并与临床 监测 数据保持一致。新颖之处在于 WVAL 系统的扩展,包括 RSV 和甲型流感。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果为 SARS-CoV-2、甲型流感和 RSV 的公共废水 监测 提供了更加一致的框架,可以为公共卫生决策提供信息并提高病毒活动监测的准确性。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于摘要证据,并且使用截至 2025 年 3 月 22 日的数据验证了该方法。这些证据支持更新的呼吸道病毒 WVAL 方法具有中等到高可信度。

title: Impact of an educational intervention on the knowledge and acceptance of RSV vaccine among Thai pregnant women: a randomized controlled trial
abstract: Abstract Background Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of acute lower respiratory tract infections in infants globally. Maternal RSV vaccination is an effective preventive strategy; however, acceptance remains uncertain in many settings. This study aimed to evaluate a video-based educational intervention on willingness to accept maternal RSV vaccination among pregnant women in Thailand. Methods In a randomized controlled trial at King Chulalongkorn Memorial Hospital (December 2025 to February 2026), eligible pregnant women were randomized to receive either a 5-minute educational video on the maternal RSV vaccine plus routine antenatal care (intervention), or routine antenatal care alone (control). Questionnaires assessed vaccine acceptance, knowledge, attitudes, and barriers at baseline, immediately post-intervention, and follow-up. The primary outcome was willingness to accept maternal RSV vaccination. Secondary outcomes included changes in RSV-related knowledge and perceptions. Outcomes were compared between groups. Both outcomes were analyzed using parametric and non-parametric statistics, while the factors associated with vaccine acceptance were evaluated using multivariable logistic regression. Results Of 410 randomized participants, 383 participants completed follow-up (intervention n = 195; control n = 188). Baseline willingness to accept vaccination was similar (intervention: 67.2% vs. control: 71.8%; p = 0.33). In the intervention group, willingness increased immediately after viewing the video from 67.2% to 82.6% (increase 15.4%, 95% CI: 8.6%-23.2%). However, no significant between-group difference was observed at follow-up (78.5% vs. The intervention group had significantly higher post-intervention knowledge scores (mean ± SD: 5.1 ± 1.3 vs. 4.7 ± 1.5; p = 0.02). Baseline acceptance, high knowledge, occupation and positive attitudes were independent predictors of willingness. Common barriers to vaccine acceptance included cost, lack of government support, and safety concerns. Conclusion A brief video intervention can improve knowledge and produce an immediate increase in willingness but did not significantly increase acceptance at follow-up. Therefore, educational interventions should be combined with strategies addressing safety concerns, provider recommendations, and financial accessibility to maximize maternal RSV vaccine uptake. Trial registration The trial was retrospectively registered with the Thai Clinical Trials Registry (Registration Number: TCTR20251226003 https://www.thaiclinicaltrials.org/show/TCTR20251226003 ). The trial was first registered on December 16, 2025, and approved on December 26, 2025. It was conducted and reported in accordance with the Consolidated Standards of Reporting Trials (CONSORT) 2025 Statement.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项研究是一项随机对照试验,于 2025 年 12 月至 2026 年 2 月在朱拉隆功国王纪念医院进行,涉及 410 名孕妇,随机接受关于母亲 RSV 疫苗 的 5 分钟教育视频加常规产前护理或仅接受常规产前护理。

analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 简短的视频干预可以提高知识并立即提高意愿,但并不能显着提高后续的接受度。基线接受度、高知识、职业和积极态度是意愿的独立预测因素。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,教育干预措施可以增强接受孕产妇 RSV 疫苗接种 的知识和意愿,但需要解决安全问题、提供者建议和财务可及性的其他策略来提高 疫苗 的吸收。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 所提供的证据并未报告研究设计的具体局限性。由于该研究是一项随机对照试验,随访率相对较高,但随访时组间无显着差异,因此证据强度中等。

title: ANTIBIOTIC PRESCRIBING IN RSV POSITIVE CHILDREN AGED OVER TWO YEARS: A SINGLE-CENTRE RETROSPECTIVE AUDIT
abstract: Background: Bronchiolitis is a common viral lower respiratory tract infection predominantly affecting children under two years of age, with Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) responsible for up to 80% of cases in the United Kingdom. Diagnosis is primarily clinical, with children presenting with coryzal symptoms progressing to cough, feeding difficulty and fever. NICE recommends supportive care as the primary treatment and advises against the routine use of antibiotics, steroids, inhaled bronchodilators, and chest X-rays, yet non-adherence to these recommendations persists in clinical practice. In older children, diagnostic certainty is further reduced and RSV positivity alone does not confirm bronchiolitis, creating both a clinical and antimicrobial stewardship challenge in an age group where limited age-specific guidance creates further clinical uncertainty. NICE recommends considering other diagnoses, including viral-induced wheeze or early-onset asthma in this age group, particularly where there is recurrent wheeze, absence of crackles, or a personal or family history of atopy. This audit aimed to evaluate whether RSV-positive children aged over two years were managed supportively, and if prescribed antibiotics, to identify clinical factors associated with antibiotic prescribing in this cohort. Methods: A single-center retrospective audit was conducted at the Royal Devon and Exeter Hospital, United Kingdom. In total, 83 patients aged over two years who tested RSV-positive and presented to the pediatric department between October 2024 and February 2025 were identified via the EPIC electronic patient record system. Data were extracted on demographics, risk factors, clinical presentation, investigations, management, and outcomes. Results: 44.6% of RSV-positive children aged over two years were prescribed antibiotics, despite NICE recommending supportive care as the primary approach to treatment. 45.8% of patients required inpatient admission. Fever (64.9%), respiratory distress (59.5%), and chest X-ray findings were the clinical findings most strongly associated with antibiotic prescribing. Notably, 51.4% of antibiotic-prescribed patients had a chest X-ray performed despite this not being routinely recommended by NICE, with 94.7% showing abnormalities. Such findings are well recognized to mimic pneumonia rather than confirm it, and should not be used to guide antibiotic prescribing in suspected bronchiolitis. Critically, 70.3% of patients prescribed antibiotics had no blood tests performed, meaning the majority of prescriptions were made without any supporting inflammatory markers. 62.1% of antibiotic prescriptions were initiated by Tier 1 clinicians. Broader guideline non-adherence was also evident, with 42.2% of patients receiving inhalers or nebulizers and 31.3% receiving steroids, neither of which is routinely recommended by NICE in bronchiolitis. Conclusions: This audit reveals substantial guideline non-adherence in the management of RSV-positive children aged over two years, with nearly half receiving antibiotics, many without objective evidence of bacterial infection. Diagnostic uncertainty in this age group, where bronchiolitis, viral-induced wheeze, and early-onset asthma overlap, is a key driver, but cannot alone account for the breadth of non-adherence observed. Key recommendations arising from this audit include the following. Targeted education for Tier 1 clinicians on differential diagnosis, antimicrobial stewardship, and the appropriate use of investigations in this age group is recommended. Antibiotic prescribing should be supported by documented clinical justification, and improved recording of atopy history, smoking exposure, and examination findings will be essential for future audit cycles. These findings highlight a broader challenge in paediatric antimicrobial stewardship: diagnostic uncertainty, without targeted education and clear local guidance, risks driving antibiotic overuse in a population where the evidence base remains limited.

source_records.abstract: Background: Bronchiolitis is a common viral lower respiratory tract infection predominantly affecting children under two years of age, with Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) responsible for up to 80% of cases in the United Kingdom. Diagnosis is primarily clinical, with children presenting with coryzal symptoms progressing to cough, feeding difficulty and fever. NICE recommends supportive care as the primary treatment and advises against the routine use of antibiotics, steroids, inhaled bronchodilators, and chest X-rays, yet non-adherence to these recommendations persists in clinical practice. In older children, diagnostic certainty is further reduced and RSV positivity alone does not confirm bronchiolitis, creating both a clinical and antimicrobial stewardship challenge in an age group where limited age-specific guidance creates further clinical uncertainty. NICE recommends considering other diagnoses, including viral-induced wheeze or early-onset asthma in this age group, particularly where there is recurrent wheeze, absence of crackles, or a personal or family history of atopy. This audit aimed to evaluate whether RSV-positive children aged over two years were managed supportively, and if prescribed antibiotics, to identify clinical factors associated with antibiotic prescribing in this cohort. Methods: A single-center retrospective audit was conducted at the Royal Devon and Exeter Hospital, United Kingdom. In total, 83 patients aged over two years who tested RSV-positive and presented to the pediatric department between October 2024 and February 2025 were identified via the EPIC electronic patient record system. Data were extracted on demographics, risk factors, clinical presentation, investigations, management, and outcomes. Results: 44.6% of RSV-positive children aged over two years were prescribed antibiotics, despite NICE recommending supportive care as the primary approach to treatment. 45.8% of patients required inpatient admission. Fever (64.9%), respiratory distress (59.5%), and chest X-ray findings were the clinical findings most strongly associated with antibiotic prescribing. Notably, 51.4% of antibiotic-prescribed patients had a chest X-ray performed despite this not being routinely recommended by NICE, with 94.7% showing abnormalities. Such findings are well recognized to mimic pneumonia rather than confirm it, and should not be used to guide antibiotic prescribing in suspected bronchiolitis. Critically, 70.3% of patients prescribed antibiotics had no blood tests performed, meaning the majority of prescriptions were made without any supporting inflammatory markers. 62.1% of antibiotic prescriptions were initiated by Tier 1 clinicians. Broader guideline non-adherence was also evident, with 42.2% of patients receiving inhalers or nebulizers and 31.3% receiving steroids, neither of which is routinely recommended by NICE in bronchiolitis. Conclusions: This audit reveals substantial guideline non-adherence in the management of RSV-positive children aged over two years, with nearly half receiving antibiotics, many without objective evidence of bacterial infection. Diagnostic uncertainty in this age group, where bronchiolitis, viral-induced wheeze, and early-onset asthma overlap, is a key driver, but cannot alone account for the breadth of non-adherence observed. Key recommendations arising from this audit include the following. Targeted education for Tier 1 clinicians on differential diagnosis, antimicrobial stewardship, and the appropriate use of investigations in this age group is recommended. Antibiotic prescribing should be supported by documented clinical justification, and improved recording of atopy history, smoking exposure, and examination findings will be essential for future audit cycles. These findings highlight a broader challenge in paediatric antimicrobial stewardship: diagnostic uncertainty, without targeted education and clear local guidance, risks driving antibiotic overuse in a population where the evidence base remains limited.

abstract_zh: 背景:毛细支气管炎是一种常见的病毒性下呼吸道感染,主要影响2岁以下儿童,在英国由呼吸道合胞病毒(呼吸道合胞病毒,RSV)引起的病例高达80%。诊断主要表现为临床症状,儿童通常出现流涕症状,随后发展为咳嗽、进食困难和发热。NICE建议将支持性治疗作为治疗的主要治疗方式,并不推荐常规使用抗生素、类固醇、吸入性支气管扩张剂和胸部X光检查,但临床实践中仍存在对这些建议的不遵守现象。在较大儿童中,诊断的确定性进一步降低,RSV阳性本身并不能确认毛细支气管炎,这在缺乏年龄特异性指导的群体中,造成了临床和抗菌药物使用管理的挑战。NICE建议在这一年龄组中考虑其他诊断,包括病毒性诱发喘息或早发性哮喘,特别是在存在反复喘息、无湿啰音或个人或家族过敏史的情况下。本次审计旨在评估年龄超过2岁的RSV阳性儿童是否接受了支持性治疗,并在开具抗生素的情况下,确定与抗生素处方相关的临床因素。方法:在英国皇家德文郡和埃克塞特医院进行了一项单中心回顾性审计。通过EPIC电子病历系统,共识别出83名年龄超过2岁且RSV阳性的儿科患者,这些患者于2024年10月至2025年2月期间就诊于儿科部门。提取了有关人口统计学、危险因素、临床表现、检查、治疗和结果的数据。结果:44.6%的年龄超过2岁的RSV阳性儿童接受了抗生素治疗,尽管NICE建议将支持性治疗作为治疗的主要方法。45.8%的患者需要住院治疗。发热(64.9%)、呼吸窘迫(59.5%)和胸部X光检查结果是与抗生素处方最显著相关的临床发现。值得注意的是,51.4%的接受抗生素治疗的患者进行了胸部X光检查,尽管NICE并未推荐常规进行此类检查,其中94.7%的检查结果异常。这些发现已被广泛认为是模拟肺炎而非确诊肺炎,不应用于指导疑似毛细支气管炎的抗生素处方。关键的是,70.3%的接受抗生素治疗的患者未进行血液检查,这意味着大多数处方是在没有任何支持性炎症标志物的情况下开具的。62.1%的抗生素处方是由Tier 1临床医生开具的。此外,还存在更广泛的指南不遵守现象,42.2%的患者接受了吸入器或雾化器治疗,31.3%的患者接受了类固醇治疗,而NICE并未推荐在毛细支气管炎中常规使用这些药物。结论:本次审计揭示了年龄超过2岁的RSV阳性儿童管理中存在显著的指南不遵守现象,近一半的患者接受了抗生素治疗,其中许多患者缺乏细菌感染的客观证据。在这一年龄组中,由于毛细支气管炎、病毒性诱发喘息和早发性哮喘的重叠,诊断的不确定性是主要驱动因素,但无法单独解释观察到的广泛不遵守现象。本次审计得出的关键建议如下。建议对Tier 1临床医生进行针对性教育,以提高对差异性诊断、抗菌药物管理以及在这一年龄组中适当使用检查的认识。抗生素处方应有明确的临床依据记录,并且未来审计周期中需要改善对过敏史、吸烟暴露和体检结果的记录。这些发现突显了儿科抗菌药物管理中的更广泛挑战:在缺乏针对性教育和明确本地指导的情况下,诊断的不确定性可能导致抗生素的过度使用,而这一人群的证据基础仍然有限。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在评估两年内 RSV 阳性儿童的管理,解决诊断 毛细支气管炎 时临床不确定性的挑战,以及持续不遵守 NICE 指南建议支持性护理而非常规抗生素使用的问题。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 英国皇家德文郡和埃克塞特医院进行了一项单中心回顾性审核,涉及 83 名年龄超过 2 岁、RSV 检测呈阳性并于 2024 年 10 月至 2025 年 2 月期间到儿科就诊的患者。
analysis_zh.methods: 提取了有关人口统计、风险因素、临床表现、调查、管理和结果的数据,重点关注抗生素处方实践和相关临床因素。
analysis_zh.main_results: 尽管 NICE 指南建议支持性护理,但 44.6% 的两岁以上 RSV 阳性儿童仍服用了抗生素。此外,45.8%的患者需要住院,51.4%的患者进行了胸部X光检查,其中94.7%的患者显示异常。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 审计强调,在两年多的时间里,在管理 RSV 阳性儿童方面,严重不遵守 NICE 指南,许多抗生素处方缺乏细菌感染的客观证据。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现强调了临床医生需要进行有针对性的抗菌药物管理教育,以及对 RSV 阳性儿童进行准确的 诊断 以减少不必要的抗生素使用的重要性。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于单中心回顾性审核,可能会影响普适性。证据是中等的,因为它是基于观察数据而不是实验或前瞻性研究。

title: AN AUDIT OF UNNECESSARY CHEST X-RAY USE IN CHILDREN UNDER 2 YEARS WITH BRONCHIOLITIS IN A DISTRICT GENERAL HOSPITAL PAEDIATRIC EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT
abstract: Background: Bronchiolitis is a common lower respiratory tract infection most commonly due to RSV with peak incidence in infants less than a year old, 1.5-2 times more common in boys than girls. It is typically self-limiting and requires solely supportive management, however, in some cases, acute complications such as bacterial infection, respiratory distress, hypoxia and apnoea may occur, requiring admission or medical management. Sequelae can also arise such as recurrent wheeze and asthma. Less experienced or informed health professionals may be tempted to investigate and manage like adults, and this can lead to the over-use of chest x-rays in children and avoidable exposure to radiation. The National Institute of Clinical Excellence (NICE) in England have published guidelines in bronchiolitis management however adherence is lacking. “Do not routinely perform a chest x-ray in children with bronchiolitis.” - NICE. Methods: Retrospective clinical audit of infants aged 0-24 months who presented to Paediatric Emergency Department at Royal Albert Edward Infirmary A&E between January 2026 and April 2026 in first presentation of illness with a clinical diagnosis of bronchiolitis were included. 130 out of 171 met the criteria. Exclusion criteria included those with supplemental oxygen requirements, severe respiratory distress, significant comorbidity such as chronic lung disease, immunodeficiency, neuromuscular disorders, congenital heart disease and previous CXR for the same illness within 2 weeks. Assessing those who received CXR and why, who reviewed, whether they were admitted and clinical uncertainty. Results: 16 out of 130 ( 12.3%) of patients received chest x-rays, 12 out of 130 ( 9.2%) were admitted. Of those who received chest x-rays,11 out of 16 ( 68.8% ) had no justifiable reason as per criteria set out by NICE guidelines. There was diagnostic uncertainty in 20% of cases. First assessor level was resident doctor in 81.4% of cases. Of the chest x-rays performed, 75% were reported normal. 81.8% of unjustified chest x-rays were reported as normal, meanwhile 60% of justified CXR’s were normal. Two abnormalities noted within the unjustified category: 1. Bilateral mild peri bronchial wall thickening. Otherwise, No focal lung lesions. Small ill-defined right paracardial patchy opacity could suggest early infective process. Otherwise, no focal lung lesions. Two abnormalities noted within the justified category: 1. Right retrocardiac and Right lower zonal increased opacification silhouetting Right hemidiaphragm likely infective. Mild peri-bronchial cuffing suggesting small airways inflammation. There was a strong positive correlation between those who received CXR and those who were admitted φ = 0.528, p=0.0000031. A statistically significant moderate correlation existed between those who received a CXR and diagnostic uncertainty p=0.0006 . While first assessor was commonly resident, there was no statistical correlation (p=0.1915). See Reason for CXR table (Table 1). Conclusions: 87.7% did not receive chest x-rays. Which reflects sound clinical judgment in the majority of cases, but this is below the 100% target. Some potential reasons may be clinical uncertainty, in which case a CXR can help differentiate. This audit revealed level of confidence was more likely the reason for CXR request than assessor level.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on the unnecessary use of chest x-rays in children under 2 years with bronchiolitis, specifically examining the frequency of chest x-ray use, reasons for its use, and the correlation with admission and diagnostic uncertainty. The central question is whether chest x-rays are appropriately used in this pediatric population.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review conducted a retrospective clinical audit of infants aged 0-24 months who presented to the Paediatric Emergency Department at Royal Albert Edward Infirmary A&E between January 2026 and April 2026. The audit included patients with a clinical diagnosis of bronchiolitis, excluding those with supplemental oxygen requirements, severe respiratory distress, significant comorbidity, or previous CXR within 2 weeks. The methods involved assessing the reasons for chest x-ray requests, assessor levels, admission status, and diagnostic uncertainty.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The audit found that 12.3% of patients received chest x-rays, with 68.8% of these having no justifiable reason according to NICE guidelines. Additionally, 75% of chest x-rays were reported as normal, and there was a strong positive correlation between chest x-ray use and admission (φ = 0.528, p=0.0000031). The level of confidence was more likely the reason for chest x-ray requests than the assessor level.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: There was a statistically significant moderate correlation between chest x-ray use and diagnostic uncertainty (p=0.0006). However, the review does not provide detailed information on the specific diagnostic uncertainties or the impact of these uncertainties on clinical decision-making. The study also does not explore the potential consequences of unnecessary chest x-ray use in terms of radiation exposure or cost-effectiveness.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The audit highlights the need for improved adherence to NICE guidelines to reduce unnecessary chest x-ray use in children with bronchiolitis. It suggests that further research should focus on understanding the reasons for diagnostic uncertainty and developing strategies to improve clinical judgment in such cases. Additionally, there is a need for better education and training for health professionals to ensure appropriate use of imaging in this population.

analysis.summary_en: This review presents a clinical audit of chest x-ray use in children under 2 years with bronchiolitis, conducted at a district general hospital. The study found that 12.3% of patients received chest x-rays, with 68.8% of these being unjustified according to NICE guidelines. A strong positive correlation was observed between chest x-ray use and admission, while diagnostic uncertainty was moderately correlated with x-ray use. The audit emphasizes the importance of adhering to clinical guidelines to minimize unnecessary radiation exposure and highlights the need for further research and training to improve diagnostic confidence and clinical decision-making in this pediatric population.

elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 本次回顾性临床审计审查了2026年1月至2026年4月期间在皇家爱德华医院急诊科就诊的0-24个月婴儿,包括临床诊断为毛细支气管炎的患者,排除了需要补充氧气、严重呼吸窘迫、有显著合并症或过去2周内有胸部X光检查记录的患者。审计方法涉及评估胸部X光检查请求的原因、评估者级别、入院状态和诊断不确定性。

abstract_zh: 背景:毛细支气管炎 是一种常见的下呼吸道感染,最常见的原因是 RSV,在一岁以下的婴儿中峰值为 发病率,男孩的发病率是女孩的 1.5-2 倍。它通常是自限性的,仅需要支持性治疗,但在某些情况下,可能会出现细菌感染、呼吸窘迫、缺氧和呼吸暂停等急性并发症,需要入院或进行医疗治疗。还可能出现后遗症,例如反复喘息和哮喘。经验不足或消息灵通的卫生专业人员可能会像成年人一样进行调查和管理,这可能导致儿童过度使用胸部 X 光检查以及本可避免的辐射暴露。英国国家临床卓越研究所 (NICE) 发布了 毛细支气管炎 管理指南,但缺乏遵守情况。“不要对患有 毛细支气管炎 的儿童进行常规胸部 X 光检查。” - 好的。方法:对 2026 年 1 月至 2026 年 4 月期间首次就诊且临床症状为 诊断 的临床 毛细支气管炎 到皇家阿尔伯特爱德华医院急症室儿科急诊科就诊的 0-24 个月婴儿进行回顾性临床审核。171 人中有 130 人符合标准。排除标准包括需要补充氧气、严重呼吸窘迫、患有慢性肺病、免疫缺陷、神经肌肉疾病、先天性心脏病等重大合并症以及两周内曾因相同疾病接受过 CXR 检查的患者。评估接受 CXR 的患者及其原因、谁进行了检查、是否入院以及临床不确定性。结果:130 名患者中有 16 名(12.3%)接受了胸部 X 光检查,130 名患者中有 12 名(9.2%)入院。根据 NICE 指南规定的标准,在接受胸部 X 光检查的人中,16 人中有 11 人(68.8%)没有正当理由。20% 的病例存在诊断不确定性。81.4%的病例第一评估级别为住院医生。在进行的胸部 X 光检查中,75% 的结果显示正常。81.8% 的不合理胸部 X 光检查报告为正常,同时 60% 的合理 CXR 报告为正常。在不合理的类别中注意到两个异常: 1. 双侧支气管周围壁轻度增厚。否则,无局灶性肺部病变。右心旁心旁小片状不明确的斑片状混浊可能提示早期感染过程。否则,肺部无局灶性病变。合理类别中注意到两个异常: 1. 右心后和右下区混浊轮廓增加 右半膈可能感染。轻微的支气管周围袖带提示小气道炎症。接受 CXR 的患者与入院患者之间存在很强的正相关性 φ = 0.528,p=0.0000031。接受 CXR 的患者与诊断不确定性 p=0.0006 之间存在统计显着的中等相关性。虽然第一位评估员通常是居民,但不存在统计相关性 (p=0.1915)。请参阅 CXR 表的原因(表 1)。结论:87.7% 的人没有接受胸部 X 光检查。这反映了大多数情况下合理的临床判断,但这低于 100% 的目标。一些潜在的原因可能是临床不确定性,在这种情况下 CXR 可以帮助区分。此次审计显示,信心级别更有可能是 CXR 请求的原因,而不是评估员级别。

analysis_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述重点关注 2 岁以下 毛细支气管炎 儿童不必要的胸部 X 光检查,特别检查胸部 X 光检查的使用频率、使用原因以及与入院和诊断不确定性的相关性。核心问题是胸部 X 光检查是否适合该儿科人群。
analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 本次回顾性临床审计审查了2026年1月至2026年4月期间在皇家爱德华医院急诊科就诊的0-24个月婴儿,包括临床诊断为毛细支气管炎的患者,排除了需要补充氧气、严重呼吸窘迫、有显著合并症或过去2周内有胸部X光检查记录的患者。审计方法涉及评估胸部X光检查请求的原因、评估者级别、入院状态和诊断不确定性。
analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 审计发现,12.3%的患者接受了胸部X光检查,其中68.8%的患者没有按照NICE指南的正当理由接受了胸部X光检查。此外,75% 的胸部 X 光检查结果显示正常,并且胸部 X 光检查的使用与入院之间存在很强的正相关性 (φ = 0.528,p=0.0000031)。信心水平更有可能是要求进行胸部 X 光检查的原因,而不是评估者水平。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 胸部 X 光检查的使用与诊断不确定性之间存在统计学上显着的中度相关性 (p=0.0006)。然而,该综述并未提供有关具体诊断不确定性或这些不确定性对临床决策影响的详细信息。该研究也没有探讨不必要的胸部 X 光检查在辐射暴露或成本效益方面的潜在后果。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 此次审计强调需要更好地遵守 NICE 指南,以减少 毛细支气管炎 儿童不必要的胸部 X 光检查。它表明进一步的研究应侧重于了解诊断不确定性的原因并制定策略以改善此类病例的临床判断。此外,需要对卫生专业人员进行更好的教育和培训,以确保在这一人群中适当使用成像技术。

title: Mucosal Vaccines Against Respiratory Viral Infections in Children: Current Advances, Challenges and Future Perspectives
abstract: Respiratory viral infections remain a leading cause of morbidity, hospitalization, and healthcare burden among children worldwide. While traditional injectable vaccines have been effective in preventing severe disease, they are often limited in their ability to induce strong mucosal immunity at the initial sites of viral entry. Mucosal vaccination has therefore been proposed as a promising strategy to improve local and systemic immune responses and to potentially decrease pathogen transmission. The aim of this study is to review recent advances in mucosal vaccine development for pediatric populations, with an emphasis on the immunological basis of mucosal protection, features related to the age of the developing immune system, and the most relevant vaccine platforms, including intranasal, oral, viral-vectored, and nanoparticle-based approaches. We discuss recent advances in mucosal vaccine development against the main respiratory viral pathogens affecting children, including respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), influenza viruses, and SARS-CoV-2, and review available preclinical and clinical evidence to support their use. Finally, we present major challenges limiting the widespread implementation of mucosal vaccines in pediatric populations, including safety, variability of immune responses, and regulatory considerations. We conclude by highlighting future directions and emerging technologies that may aid the development of safe, effective, and long-lasting mucosal vaccination strategies for the prevention of respiratory viral infections in children.

title_zh: 粘膜 疫苗 对抗儿童呼吸道病毒感染:当前进展、挑战和未来前景
source_body_en: Respiratory viral infections remain a leading cause of morbidity, hospitalization, and healthcare burden among children worldwide. While traditional injectable vaccines have been effective in preventing severe disease, they are often limited in their ability to induce strong mucosal immunity at the initial sites of viral entry. Mucosal vaccination has therefore been proposed as a promising strategy to improve local and systemic immune responses and to potentially decrease pathogen transmission. The aim of this study is to review recent advances in mucosal vaccine development for pediatric populations, with an emphasis on the immunological basis of mucosal protection, features related to the age of the developing immune system, and the most relevant vaccine platforms, including intranasal, oral, viral-vectored, and nanoparticle-based approaches. We discuss recent advances in mucosal vaccine development against the main respiratory viral pathogens affecting children, including respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), influenza viruses, and SARS-CoV-2, and review available preclinical and clinical evidence to support their use. Finally, we present major challenges limiting the widespread implementation of mucosal vaccines in pediatric populations, including safety, variability of immune responses, and regulatory considerations. We conclude by highlighting future directions and emerging technologies that may aid the development of safe, effective, and long-lasting mucosal vaccination strategies for the prevention of respiratory viral infections in children.
abstract_zh: 呼吸道病毒感染仍然是全世界儿童发病、住院和医疗负担的主要原因。虽然传统的注射剂 疫苗 可有效预防严重疾病,但它们在病毒进入初始部位诱导强烈粘膜免疫的能力往往受到限制。因此,粘膜 疫苗接种 被认为是改善局部和全身 免疫应答 并潜在减少病原体 传播 的有前途的策略。本研究的目的是回顾儿科人群粘膜 疫苗 发育的最新进展,重点是粘膜保护的免疫学基础、与免疫系统发育年龄相关的特征以及最相关的 疫苗 平台,包括鼻内、口服、病毒载体和基于纳米颗粒的方法。我们讨论了粘膜 疫苗 针对影响儿童的主要呼吸道病毒病原体(包括 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV)、流感病毒和 SARS-CoV-2)的最新进展,并回顾了现有的临床前和临床证据以支持其使用。最后,我们提出了限制粘膜 疫苗 在儿科人群中广泛实施的主要挑战,包括安全性、免疫应答 的变异性和监管考虑。最后,我们强调未来的方向和新兴技术可能有助于开发安全、有效和持久的粘膜 疫苗接种 策略来预防儿童呼吸道病毒感染。

title: GUT MICROBIOTA PATTERNS IN PEDIATRIC RESPIRATORY INFECTIONS: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW OF MICROBIAL SIGNATURES
abstract: Early-life gut microbiota plays a crucial role in immune maturation and has been increasingly associated with host responses to infectious diseases. Emerging evidence highlights the gut–lung axis as an important component of pediatric respiratory health, yet child-focused syntheses remain limited. This systematic review with qualitative analysis summarizes recent original studies evaluating gut microbiota profiles in children with acute respiratory infections, providing a child-specific perspective distinct from reviews that combine age groups or focus on single pathogens. PubMed and the Virtual Health Library were systematically searched and the data were extracted using a structured matrix to identify patterns in microbial composition and methodological strengths and gaps. Twelve studies (2019–2025) including participants aged 0–18 years with conditions such as COVID-19, respiratory syncytial virus infection, bronchiolitis, and recurrent respiratory tract infections met predefined inclusion criteria. Across studies, children with respiratory infections consistently exhibited gut dysbiosis, characterized by depletion of beneficial taxa and enrichment of pro-inflammatory genera. While methodological differences, including study design, sampling timing, and handling of confounders, limited direct quantitative comparisons, patterns of microbial alterations were identifiable. Overall, this review highlights a consistent association between gut microbiota alterations and pediatric respiratory infections, supporting the relevance of the gut–lung axis in early life. Nevertheless, methodological heterogeneity prevents inference about cause-and-effect relationships, highlighting the need for well-designed longitudinal and interventional studies to better understand the directionality of these associations.

analysis.scope_and_question: This review focuses on the gut microbiota patterns in children with respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection, specifically examining microbial signatures associated with RSV bronchiolitis and RSV infection. The central question is how gut microbiota alterations are linked to pediatric respiratory infections, particularly RSV-related conditions, and their role in immune responses.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review conducted a systematic search of PubMed and the Virtual Health Library, covering studies from 2019 to 2025. Data were extracted using a structured matrix to identify patterns in microbial composition and methodological strengths and gaps. The review included twelve studies with participants aged 0–18 years.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Across the twelve studies, children with RSV infections consistently exhibited gut dysbiosis, characterized by depletion of beneficial taxa and enrichment of pro-inflammatory genera. This supports the relevance of the gut–lung axis in early life and highlights a consistent association between gut microbiota alterations and pediatric respiratory infections.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Methodological heterogeneity, including variations in study design, sampling timing, and handling of confounders, limited direct quantitative comparisons. This prevents inference about cause-and-effect relationships, indicating a need for more standardized and longitudinal studies to better understand the directionality of these associations.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review emphasizes the importance of well-designed longitudinal and interventional studies to explore the causal relationships between gut microbiota and RSV infections. It also suggests the need for further research on microbial signatures in pediatric respiratory infections to inform targeted interventions and improve clinical outcomes.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review explores the gut microbiota patterns in children with respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection, focusing on microbial signatures associated with RSV bronchiolitis and RSV infection. The review highlights a consistent association between gut dysbiosis and RSV-related respiratory conditions, emphasizing the role of the gut–lung axis in immune responses. However, methodological differences across studies limit direct quantitative comparisons and prevent causal inferences. The findings underscore the need for more standardized, longitudinal, and interventional research to better understand the relationship between gut microbiota and RSV infections, with potential implications for targeted interventions and improved clinical outcomes in pediatric populations.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 本综述重点关注 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 感染儿童的肠道微生物群模式,特别检查与 RSV 毛细支气管炎 和 RSV 感染相关的微生物特征。核心问题是肠道微生物群的改变如何与儿童呼吸道感染(特别是 RSV 相关疾病)相关,以及它们在 免疫应答 中的作用。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述对 PubMed 和虚拟健康图书馆进行了系统检索,涵盖 2019 年至 2025 年的研究。使用结构化矩阵提取数据,以确定微生物组成模式以及方法学优势和差距。该综述包括 12 项研究,参与者年龄为 0-18 岁。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 在这 12 项研究中,RSV 感染的儿童始终表现出肠道菌群失调,其特征是有益类群的消耗和促炎菌属的富集。这支持了生命早期肠肺轴的相关性,并强调了肠道微生物群改变与儿童呼吸道感染之间的一致关联。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 方法学异质性,包括研究设计、采样时间和混杂因素处理的差异,限制了直接定量比较。这阻碍了对因果关系的推断,表明需要进行更标准化和纵向的研究,以更好地理解这些关联的方向性。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 该综述强调了精心设计的纵向和介入研究的重要性,以探索肠道微生物群与 RSV 感染之间的因果关系。它还表明需要对儿科呼吸道感染的微生物特征进行进一步研究,以便为有针对性的干预措施提供信息并改善临床结果。

abstract_zh: 生命早期的肠道微生物群在免疫成熟中发挥着至关重要的作用,并且与 宿主 对传染病的反应越来越相关。新的证据强调肠肺轴是儿科呼吸健康的重要组成部分,但以儿童为中心的综合仍然有限。这篇带有定性分析的系统综述总结了最近评估急性呼吸道感染儿童肠道微生物群概况的原始研究,提供了与结合年龄组或关注单一病原体的综述不同的针对儿童的视角。对 PubMed 和虚拟健康图书馆进行了系统搜索,并使用结构化矩阵提取数据,以确定微生物组成的模式以及方法学的优势和差距。12 项研究(2019-2025)包括年龄为 0-18 岁、患有 COVID-19、呼吸道合胞病毒 感染、毛细支气管炎 和复发性呼吸道感染等疾病的参与者,这些研究符合预定的纳入标准。各项研究中,患有呼吸道感染的儿童始终表现出肠道菌群失调,其特征是有益类群的消耗和促炎属的富集。虽然方法上的差异,包括研究设计、采样时间和混杂因素的处理,限制了直接定量比较,但微生物改变的模式是可识别的。总的来说,这篇综述强调了肠道微生物群改变与儿童呼吸道感染之间的一致关联,支持了早期生命中肠-肺轴的相关性。然而,方法论的异质性阻碍了对因果关系的推断,凸显了需要精心设计的纵向和干预性研究,以更好地理解这些关联的方向性。

analysis_zh.scope_and_question: 本综述重点关注 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 感染儿童的肠道微生物群模式,特别检查与 RSV 毛细支气管炎 和 RSV 感染相关的微生物特征。核心问题是肠道微生物群的改变如何与儿童呼吸道感染(特别是 RSV 相关疾病)相关,以及它们在 免疫应答 中的作用。
analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述对 PubMed 和虚拟健康图书馆进行了系统检索,涵盖 2019 年至 2025 年的研究。使用结构化矩阵提取数据,以确定微生物组成模式以及方法学优势和差距。该综述包括 12 项研究,参与者年龄为 0-18 岁。
analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 在这 12 项研究中,RSV 感染的儿童始终表现出肠道菌群失调,其特征是有益类群的消耗和促炎菌属的富集。这支持了生命早期肠肺轴的相关性,并强调了肠道微生物群改变与儿童呼吸道感染之间的一致关联。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 方法学异质性,包括研究设计、采样时间和混杂因素处理的差异,限制了直接定量比较。这阻碍了对因果关系的推断,表明需要进行更标准化和纵向的研究,以更好地理解这些关联的方向性。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 该综述强调了精心设计的纵向和介入研究的重要性,以探索肠道微生物群与 RSV 感染之间的因果关系。它还表明需要对儿科呼吸道感染的微生物特征进行进一步研究,以便为有针对性的干预措施提供信息并改善临床结果。
