title: MATERNAL RSV VACCINATION AND CLINICAL SEVERITY OF RSV-POSITIVE BRONCHIOLITIS IN CHILDREN ADMITTED TO THE PAEDIATRIC WARD: A RETROSPECTIVE OBSERVATIONAL STUDY
abstract: Background Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is the leading cause of bronchiolitis requiring hospital admission in infants. Maternal RSV vaccination was introduced in the UK in September 2024 to reduce severe RSV disease during early infancy. This retrospective study evaluated the clinical characteristics of children admitted with RSV-positive bronchiolitis in relation to maternal RSV immunisation status and the association between maternal RSV vaccination and respiratory support and length of hospital stay. Methods Children admitted with laboratory-confirmed RSV-positive bronchiolitis between October 2025 and February 2026 across two hospitals within the Trust were included in the study. Maternal RSV vaccination status was obtained from BadgerNet electronic records. Children’s data were collected from electronic patient records. Data collected included age at presentation, respiratory support, and duration of hospital stay. Respiratory support was categorised as no respiratory support, low-flow oxygen (LFO2), or high-flow nasal oxygen (AIRVO). Results A total of 97 children were admitted with RSV-positive bronchiolitis. Maternal RSV vaccination status was available for 90 children; 37 (41%) were born to vaccinated mothers and 53 (59%) to unvaccinated mothers. In the vaccinated group, 24 (64.9%) children were aged 0–6 months, 12 (32.4%) were aged 6–12 months, and only one (2.7%) was older than 12 months. In contrast, among children born to unvaccinated mothers, 19 (36%) were aged 0–6 months, 8 (15%) were aged 6–12 months, and 26 (49%) were older than 12 months. However, the number of infants younger than 2 months with RSV infection was lower in the vaccinated group than in the unvaccinated group (4 vs 11 children). Thus, among infants and children whose mothers had received the RSV vaccine, almost all admissions (97.3%) occurred before 12 months of age. In contrast, almost half of admissions (49%) in the unvaccinated group occurred in children older than 12 months. Children whose mothers had received the RSV vaccine appeared to require less respiratory support overall. The proportion requiring no respiratory support was higher in the vaccinated group than in the unvaccinated group (62.2% vs 49%). Low-flow oxygen was required in 27.0% of children in the vaccinated group compared with 36% in the unvaccinated group. Similarly, AIRVO (high-flow nasal oxygen) was required in 10.8% of children in the vaccinated group compared with 15% in the unvaccinated group. There was a statistically significant association between vaccination status and length of hospital stay (χ2 = 12.83, p = 0.0016). Children whose mother had received the vaccine were more likely to have a hospital stay of 3 days (50.9% vs 18.9%). Limitations This was an observational analysis, and potential confounding factors were not included, including prematurity, underlying comorbidities and the timing of maternal RSV vaccination. The difference in age distribution between the two groups may have influenced the results. Conclusions Children born to mothers who received the RSV vaccine appeared to require less respiratory support and had statistically significant shorter hospital stays. Fewer children in the vaccinated group appeared to require escalation to AIRVO, suggesting a potential reduction in the severity of bronchiolitis. These findings suggest an association between maternal RSV vaccination and reduced disease severity and healthcare utilisation.

analysis.summary_en: This retrospective observational study investigated the clinical characteristics of children admitted with RSV-positive bronchiolitis in relation to maternal RSV immunisation status. The study was conducted across two hospitals in the UK between October 2025 and February 2026, involving 97 children. Maternal vaccination status was available for 90 children, with 41% born to vaccinated mothers and 59% to unvaccinated mothers. elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 是婴儿 毛细支气管炎 需要入院的主要原因。本研究旨在评估 RSV 阳性 毛细支气管炎 入院儿童的临床特征与母亲 RSV 免疫状态的关系,以及母亲 RSV 毛细支气管炎 与呼吸支持和住院时间之间的关系。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项回顾性观察研究是在 2025 年 10 月至 2026 年 2 月期间在信托基金内的两家医院进行的。共有 97 名患有 RSV 阳性 毛细支气管炎 的儿童入院,其中 90 名儿童的母亲 RSV 毛细支气管炎 状态可用。
elements_zh.methods: 儿童数据从电子病历中收集,母亲 RSV 疫苗接种 状态从 BadgerNet 电子记录中获取。收集的数据包括就诊时的年龄、呼吸支持和住院时间。
elements_zh.main_results: 90 名儿童的母亲 RSV 疫苗接种 状态可用;37 例 (41%) 是接种疫苗的母亲所生,53 例 (59%) 是未接种疫苗的母亲所生。接种组中感染 RSV 的 2 个月以下婴儿数量低于未接种组(4 例 vs 11 例)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现表明母体 RSV 疫苗接种 与疾病严重程度和医疗保健利用率降低之间存在关联。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果可能为婴儿 RSV 预防和管理的未来策略提供参考,特别是关于母亲 疫苗接种 在减少呼吸支持需求和缩短住院时间方面的潜在益处。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 这是一项观察性分析,不包括潜在的混杂因素,包括早产、潜在的合并症和母体 RSV 疫苗接种 的时间。由于观察性质和缺乏对混杂变量的控制,证据是中等的。

title: Clinical and Laboratory Characteristics of RSV-Positive and RSV-Negative Bronchiolitis in Hospitalized Children Younger Than Two Years: A Comparative Cross-Sectional Study
abstract: Objective: To compare the demographic, clinical and laboratory characteristics of hospitalized children with RSV-positive and RSV-negative bronchiolitis. Methodology: This comparative cross-sectional study included 60 children younger than two years admitted with bronchiolitis to a tertiary-care hospital in Islamabad from November 2025 to April 2026. RSV status was determined by viral polymerase chain reaction (PCR), with 30 children in each group. Clinical severity was assessed using the Wood-Downes-Ferrés (WDF) score. Two-sided comparisons were recalculated from available group summaries. Results: Children with RSV-positive bronchiolitis were younger than RSV-negative children (3.9 ± 3.2 vs 8.9 ± 9.8 months; p=0.012). Cough and fever were common in both groups. More than two presenting symptoms were reported more often in the RSV-negative group (73.3% vs 43.3%; p=0.035). Mean WDF score was higher in the RSV-positive group (5.9 ± 2.2 vs 4.4 ± 2.4; p=0.014). Total leukocyte count was numerically higher (12.2 ± 3.7 vs 10.5 ± 3.1 ×109/L), although this difference was not statistically significant on recalculation (p=0.059). C-reactive protein positivity was identical in both groups (50.0%). Conclusions: Hospitalized children with RSV-positive bronchiolitis were younger and had higher unadjusted bedside respiratory severity scores. Presenting symptoms and routine blood findings overlapped substantially. No quantitative PCR viral-load information was available, and no age- or sex-stratified assessment could be reconstructed. These findings should be interpreted cautiously because age-adjusted analyses and individual severity categories were unavailable. The study describes differences between hospitalized groups rather than proving that RSV independently determines severity at the time of admission in this single-center comparison.
journal: Annals of PIMS-Shaheed Zulfiqar Ali Bhutto Medical University

title: Respiratory Pathogen Positivity in Children: Shifting Patterns at a Single Children’s Hospital in Hangzhou, China, 2024–2025
abstract: Respiratory infections are frequently encountered in children and constitute an important threat to pediatric health. Monitoring temporal shifts in the circulating pathogen spectrum is consequently important for informing effective prevention and treatment strategies. To assess changes in respiratory pathogen test positivity among tested children during 2024–2025, we examined respiratory pathogen testing data obtained from patients attending a large children’s hospital in eastern China, with results stratified according to pathogen, age group, and month of onset. abstract_zh: 呼吸道感染是儿童常见的疾病,对儿科健康构成重要威胁。因此,监测循环病原体谱的时间变化对于提供有效的预防和 治疗 策略非常重要。为了评估 2024 年至 2025 年受测儿童呼吸道病原体检测阳性的变化,我们检查了从中国东部一家大型儿童医院就诊的患者获得的呼吸道病原体检测数据,结果根据病原体、年龄组和发病月份进行分层。人鼻病毒(HRV)仍然是 2024 年(10,268/47,650;21.55%)和 2025 年(10,634/50,627;21.00%)最常见的病原体。2024年,肺炎支原体(MP)排名第二(9663/47,650;20.28%),而2025年其检出率大幅下降(1647/50,627;3.25%)。相比之下,呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV;8058/50,627;15.92%)和甲型流感病毒(InfA;4424/50,627;8.74%)在2025年变得更加突出,分别占据HRV之后的第二和第三位。1-3 岁儿童在呼吸道感染中所占比例始终较高。然而,超过 3 岁后,病原体谱发生了变化,最明显的变化是 InfA 感染与年龄相关的增加。与 2024 年相比,2025 年冬季记录的病例数也大幅增加。气候变化、疫苗接种 覆盖范围和其他因素在这些流行病学变化中的潜在作用需要进一步调查。这些单中心测试阳性结果不应被解释为受测儿童的区域阳性率。因此,儿童呼吸道感染的预防和控制措施应考虑病原体谱的变化,特别是在高危年龄组和季节性高峰期间。

title: Vaccination in Adult Patients with Inflammatory Bowel Disease: An Updated Practical Approach
abstract: PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Due to both disease-mediated and therapy-induced immunosuppression, patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) are at increased risk of infections, including from vaccine preventable diseases (VPDs). As such, prevention through vaccination is a key aspect of longitudinal care to decrease infection-associated morbidity. In this review, we aim to outline a practical approach to vaccination in patients with IBD. RECENT FINDINGS: The importance of vaccination for prevention of VPDs has been highlighted in multiple societal guideline updates. In recent years, these guidelines have expanded to include updated recommendations for coronavirus disease 2019, respiratory syncytial virus, and hepatitis B virus immunization. Additional guidance regarding use of live vaccines has also been provided. Having a practical and patient-centered approach to vaccination in patients with IBD is an important part of longitudinal care and prevention of morbidity. Herein we have highlighted risks of infection, the contributing role of immunosuppressive therapy, and comprehensively reviewed recommendations for and approach to vaccination.

title: Post-pandemic shifts in respiratory pathogens and peripheral immune correlates among hospitalized children with ALRTI: a retrospective molecular surveillance study in northern China, 2023–2024
abstract: Background Post-pandemic respiratory pathogen circulation has changed, but concurrent molecular and immune data remain limited. We examined pathogen trends and peripheral immune correlates in children hospitalized with acute lower respiratory tract infection (ALRTI) in northern China during 2023–2024. Methods This single-centre retrospective study included 604 hospitalization episodes. A 13-target multiplex nucleic-acid panel defined pathogen groups. Immunoglobulins, lymphocyte subsets and inflammatory markers were compared across monoinfection, mixed infection (≥2 pathogen categories) and panel-negative groups. Immune comparisons adjusted for age, sex and year using regression with cluster-robust standard errors for repeated admissions and false-discovery-rate correction. Annual trends were assessed using age-standardised rates and logistic regression adjusted for age, sex and calendar month. Results Among 601 complete-panel episodes, 528 (87.9%) had a detected pathogen. Mycoplasma pneumoniae predominated (43.4%), followed by rhinovirus (23.6%) and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV; 14.3%). pneumoniae detection increased from 32.4% in 2023 to 54.3% in 2024, while RSV decreased from 21.4% to 7.3% (both q < 0.001). Annual shifts persisted after age standardisation and covariate adjustment: adjusted odds ratios for 2024 vs. 2023 were 3.09 (95% CI, 1.94–4.94) for M. pneumoniae, 0.29 (0.16–0.53) for RSV and 0.13 (0.03–0.53) for influenza A. Mixed infection (21.5%) decreased with age (adjusted odds ratio per year, 0.92; 95% CI, 0.86–0.98). After adjustment and multiplicity correction, M. pneumoniae and mixed infections were associated with higher immunoglobulin M. Rhinovirus monoinfection was associated with lower total T-cell and CD8+ T-cell percentages and higher B-cell percentage; mixed infection was associated with lower total T-cell percentage. Cytokine analyses were exploratory because approximately 35% of episodes were tested. Conclusion Pathogen profiles shifted substantially between 2023 and 2024, supporting continued molecular surveillance and age-aware interpretation of immune measures. Because the panel did not cover typical bacterial pathogens, panel-negative episodes should not be equated with absence of infection.

title: Spheroids in virology: Bridging the gap between conventional 2D cultures and in vivo models
abstract: Two-dimensional cell cultures have long served as a standard tool in virological research, enabling the study of viral replication, cytopathic effects, antiviral activity, and host-pathogen interactions under controlled conditions. However, conventional monolayers often fail to reproduce the structural complexity, cellular polarity, extracellular matrix (ECM) interactions, and diffusion gradients characteristic of native tissues. This compromises their physiological relevance and predictive value, especially for viruses that depend on tissue microenvironments for replication and pathogenesis. Three-dimensional (3D) cell culture systems, including spheroids, provide an intermediate platform between simplified 2D cultures and animal models, as they better recapitulate cell-cell interactions, spatial organization, nutrient and oxygen gradients, and tissue-like responses to infection. This review examines spheroid formation techniques used in virological studies, considers the influence of spheroid architecture on viral dissemination and replication, and looks at spheroid models used in clinically relevant viruses, including influenza viruses, respiratory syncytial virus, rhinoviruses, coronaviruses, bocavirus, hepatitis viruses, and herpesviruses. The evidence reviewed suggests that spheroid systems can enhance viral propagation, model host responses, support antiviral drug screening, and offer new insights into viral pathogenesis. Spheroids represent an accessible and promising platform to advance experimental virology and close the gap between in vitro and in vivo models despite technical challenges in standardization, scalability, analysis of infection dynamics, and incomplete reproduction of tissue complexity.

title_zh: 病毒学中的球体:弥合传统 2D 培养物和体内模型之间的差距
source_body_en: Two-dimensional cell cultures have long served as a standard tool in virological research, enabling the study of viral replication, cytopathic effects, antiviral activity, and host-pathogen interactions under controlled conditions. abstract_zh: 二维细胞培养物长期以来一直作为病毒学研究的标准工具,能够在受控条件下研究病毒复制、细胞病变效应、抗病毒药物 活性和 宿主 与病原体相互作用。然而,传统的单层细胞通常无法重现天然组织的结构复杂性、细胞极性、细胞外基质 (ECM) 相互作用和扩散梯度特征。这损害了它们的生理相关性和预测价值,特别是对于依赖组织微环境进行复制和 发病机制 的病毒。三维 (3D) 细胞培养系统(包括球体)在简化的 2D 培养物和动物模型之间提供了一个中间平台,因为它们可以更好地概括细胞间相互作用、空间组织、营养和氧气梯度以及对感染的组织样反应。本综述研究了病毒学研究中使用的球体形成技术,考虑了球体结构对病毒传播和复制的影响,并研究了临床相关病毒中使用的球体模型,包括流感病毒、呼吸道合胞病毒、鼻病毒、冠状病毒、博卡病毒、肝炎病毒和疱疹病毒。审查的证据表明,球体系统可以增强病毒传播、模拟 宿主 反应、支持 抗病毒药物 药物筛选,并提供对病毒 发病机制 的新见解。尽管在标准化、可扩展性、感染动力学分析和组织复杂性的不完整再现方面存在技术挑战,但球体代表了一个可访问且有前途的平台,可推进实验病毒学并缩小体外和体内模型之间的差距。

title: Impact of Nasopharyngeal Swab Freezing Storage on the Detection of Common Respiratory Viral Molecular Targets
abstract: Archived respiratory specimens are valuable biological samples for retrospective diagnostic studies and assay validation. However, long-term storage may affect viral nucleic acid integrity and molecular detection, which is an issue of particular relevance for RNA viruses, whose RNA genomes may be particularly susceptible to storage-related degradation. The present study evaluates the quality and stability of nasopharyngeal swab (NPS) aliquots stored at −80 °C for at least one year in our biobank and subsequently retested for the same viral RNA targets. NPS previously tested for SARS-CoV-2, influenza virus, or respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) were retested using a fully automated sample-to-result molecular platform integrating nucleic acid extraction, amplification, and viral target detection in different multiplex assay formats. As the stored samples were tested using an assay different from the one used for the corresponding fresh samples, discordant results were further assessed using a third independent molecular assay. Qualitative results were compared with previous testing to assess diagnostic agreement, and changes in cycle threshold (Ct) values were analyzed. Target SARS-CoV-2 showed the highest stability, with positive percent agreement (PPA) of 97.1–98.6% and Ct increases of 2.08–3.03 cycles across assay formats. RSV showed intermediate stability, with a PPA of 88.4–97.1% and Ct increases of 1.75–5.20 cycles. Influenza showed the greatest signal loss, with PPA of 80.0–92.9% and mean Ct increases of 5.47–7.92 cycles. The Ct increases after storage were significant for all viral targets. Differences between assay configurations indicated that assay formulation and target characteristics may influence post-storage performance. Respiratory swab aliquots stored at −80° C can support retrospective molecular testing, although storage-related signal loss varies according to the viral target and assay configuration. These effects should be considered when interpreting results from archived specimens.

title: Impacto de la vacunación materna en lactantes con bronquiolitis ingresados con soporte respiratorio. Centro Hospitalario Pereira Rossell. Uruguay. Invierno, 2025
abstract: To analyze the impact of maternal vaccination against respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) perfusion protein F in infants under one year of age with bronchiolitis requiring respiratory support at the Pereira Rossell Hospital Center during the winter of 2025. An analytical, observational, longitudinal, ambispective cohort study was conducted, including infants under 12 months of age with bronchiolitis requiring respiratory support, divided into two groups according to maternal vaccination status. Clinical characteristics associated with worse disease progression and severity were analyzed. Quantitative variables were presented as medians and interquartile ranges or means and standard deviations, and qualitative variables as absolute and relative frequencies. Mann-Whitney U test, t-test, Fisher’s exact test, and chi-square test were applied, depending on the type of variable, to compare both groups (patients whose mothers were vaccinated vs. those whose mothers were not). A p-value <0.05 was considered statistically significant. Two hundred and twenty-six patients were included, mostly male (136, 60%), and 176 (79%) had RSV. The proportion of vaccinated mothers was 44 (19%). The median age was lower in patients whose mothers were vaccinated (3 months, range 2–5) vs. 5 months (range 3–9), p < 0.001. No significant differences were observed between the groups for clinical variables at admission or those associated with a worse outcome. Conclusions: The lower proportion of infants with unvaccinated mothers may suggest a greater impact of this vaccine on the risk of hospitalization. Further studies including other variables are needed for a better understanding of this strategy.

source_records.abstract: To analyze the impact of maternal vaccination against respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) perfusion protein F in infants under one year of age with bronchiolitis requiring respiratory support at the Pereira Rossell Hospital Center during the winter of 2025. An analytical, observational, longitudinal, ambispective cohort study was conducted, including infants under 12 months of age with bronchiolitis requiring respiratory support, divided into two groups according to maternal vaccination status. Clinical characteristics associated with worse disease progression and severity were analyzed. Quantitative variables were presented as medians and interquartile ranges or means and standard deviations, and qualitative variables as absolute and relative frequencies. Mann-Whitney U test, t-test, Fisher’s exact test, and chi-square test were applied, depending on the type of variable, to compare both groups (patients whose mothers were vaccinated vs. those whose mothers were not). A p-value <0.05 was considered statistically significant. Two hundred and twenty-six patients were included, mostly male (136, 60%), and 176 (79%) had RSV. The proportion of vaccinated mothers was 44 (19%). The median age was lower in patients whose mothers were vaccinated (3 months, range 2–5) vs. 5 months (range 3–9), p < 0.001. No significant differences were observed between the groups for clinical variables at admission or those associated with a worse outcome. Conclusions: The lower proportion of infants with unvaccinated mothers may suggest a greater impact of this vaccine on the risk of hospitalization. Further studies including other variables are needed for a better understanding of this strategy.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate the impact of maternal vaccination against respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) on infants under one year of age with bronchiolitis requiring respiratory support. This is relevant due to the high burden of RSV-related hospitalizations in young infants.
analysis.study_design_and_population: An observational, longitudinal, ambispective cohort study was conducted at the Pereira Rossell Hospital Center in Uruguay during the winter of 2025, including infants under 12 months of age with bronchiolitis requiring respiratory support, stratified by maternal vaccination status.
analysis.methods: The study analyzed clinical characteristics associated with disease progression and severity, using quantitative variables presented as medians and interquartile ranges or means and standard deviations, and qualitative variables as absolute and relative frequencies. Statistical tests including Mann-Whitney U test, t-test, Fisher’s exact test, and chi-square test were applied to compare the groups.
analysis.main_results: The median age was significantly lower in infants whose mothers were vaccinated (3 months, range 2–5) compared to those whose mothers were not (5 months, range 3–9), p < 0.001. No significant differences were observed between the groups for clinical variables at admission or those associated with a worse outcome.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors suggest that the lower proportion of infants with unvaccinated mothers may indicate a potential protective effect of maternal vaccination against RSV. However, they emphasize the need for further studies to better understand this strategy.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings may inform public health strategies regarding maternal vaccination to reduce the risk of RSV-related hospitalizations in infants. They highlight the importance of considering maternal vaccination status in the management of RSV bronchiolitis.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is observational and does not establish causality. The evidence is limited by the lack of control for confounding variables, and the results should be interpreted with caution due to the potential for bias.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the impact of maternal vaccination against respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) on infants under one year of age with bronchiolitis requiring respiratory support at the Pereira Rossell Hospital Center in Uruguay during the winter of 2025. It was an observational, longitudinal, ambispective cohort study comparing infants based on their mothers' vaccination status. The median age was significantly lower in vaccinated mothers' infants (3 months) compared to non-vaccinated mothers' infants (5 months), but no significant differences were observed in clinical variables at admission or outcomes. The authors suggest that maternal vaccination may reduce the risk of hospitalization, though they acknowledge the need for further studies to confirm this. The study's limitations include its observational nature and lack of control for confounding factors, which may affect the strength of the evidence.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 2025 年冬季,乌拉圭佩雷拉·罗塞尔医院中心进行了一项观察性、纵向、双重性 队列研究 研究,研究对象包括 12 个月以下、需要呼吸支持的 毛细支气管炎 婴儿,并按母亲 疫苗接种 状态进行分层。
elements_zh.methods: 该研究使用以中位数和四分位数范围或平均值和标准差表示的定量变量,以及以绝对和相对频率表示的定性变量,分析了与疾病进展和严重程度相关的临床特征。采用Mann-Whitney U检验、t检验、Fisher精确检验和卡方检验等统计检验来比较各组。
elements_zh.main_results: 与母亲未接种疫苗的婴儿(5 个月,范围 3-9)相比,母亲接种疫苗的婴儿(3 个月,范围 2-5)的婴儿中位年龄显着较低,p < 0.001。入院时的临床变量或与较差结果相关的临床变量在各组之间没有观察到显着差异。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者认为,母亲未接种疫苗的婴儿比例较低可能表明母亲 疫苗接种 对 RSV 具有潜在的保护作用。然而,他们强调需要进一步研究以更好地理解这一策略。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果可能为有关孕产妇 疫苗接种 的公共卫生策略提供信息,以降低婴儿因 RSV 相关住院的风险。他们强调了在 RSV 毛细支气管炎 管理中考虑母亲 疫苗接种 状态的重要性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究是观察性的,并未建立因果关系。由于缺乏对混杂变量的控制,证据受到限制,由于可能存在偏差,结果应谨慎解释。

title: Incremental predictive value of public surveillance indicators for RSV and influenza hospitalizations in older adults
abstract: PURPOSE: To assess whether public surveillance indicators improve forecasts of influenza- and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV)-associated hospitalizations among adults aged ≥ 65 years beyond hospitalization history and seasonality. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed U.S. FluSurv-NET and RSV-NET hospitalization rates from October 2018 through July 2026. We compared forecasts based on recent hospitalizations and seasonality with forecasts that also used older-adult emergency department (ED) percentages, all-age laboratory positivity, or national weighted influenza-like illness (wILI). Accuracy was assessed on identical forecast weeks using mean absolute error (MAE) differences and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Additional comparisons used the same historical observations and alternative seasonal curves. RESULTS: On 120 RSV forecast weeks, laboratory positivity improved MAE by 0.096 hospitalizations per 100,000 per week (95% CI 0.039-0.159). ED alone did not clearly improve forecasts (-0.059; -0.119 to 0.005), nor did ED added to laboratory positivity. On 74 influenza weeks, wILI improved MAE by 0.266 (0.064-0.567) under the primary seasonal model. Using the same historical observations preserved these principal findings. RSV laboratory gains also persisted with alternative seasonal curves, whereas the wILI estimate with a more flexible seasonal curve was 0.099 (-0.062 to 0.299). CONCLUSIONS: All-age laboratory positivity improved older-adult RSV forecasts across the examined seasonal specifications. The one-week influenza wILI increment depended on how seasonality was modeled. ED percentages provided no consistent one-week incremental benefit.

source_records.abstract: PURPOSE: To assess whether public surveillance indicators improve forecasts of influenza- and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV)-associated hospitalizations among adults aged ≥ 65 years beyond hospitalization history and seasonality. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed U.S. FluSurv-NET and RSV-NET hospitalization rates from October 2018 through July 2026. We compared forecasts based on recent hospitalizations and seasonality with forecasts that also used older-adult emergency department (ED) percentages, all-age laboratory positivity, or national weighted influenza-like illness (wILI). Accuracy was assessed on identical forecast weeks using mean absolute error (MAE) differences and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Additional comparisons used the same historical observations and alternative seasonal curves. RESULTS: On 120 RSV forecast weeks, laboratory positivity improved MAE by 0.096 hospitalizations per 100,000 per week (95% CI 0.039-0.159). ED alone did not clearly improve forecasts (-0.059; -0.119 to 0.005), nor did ED added to laboratory positivity. On 74 influenza weeks, wILI improved MAE by 0.266 (0.064-0.567) under the primary seasonal model. Using the same historical observations preserved these principal findings. RSV laboratory gains also persisted with alternative seasonal curves, whereas the wILI estimate with a more flexible seasonal curve was 0.099 (-0.062 to 0.299). CONCLUSIONS: All-age laboratory positivity improved older-adult RSV forecasts across the examined seasonal specifications. The one-week influenza wILI increment depended on how seasonality was modeled. ED percentages provided no consistent one-week incremental benefit.

abstract_zh: 目的:评估公共 监测 指标是否可以改善年龄 ≥ 65 岁且超出住院史和季节性的成人中流感和 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 相关住院的预测。方法:我们回顾性分析了 2018 年 10 月至 2026 年 7 月期间的美国 FluSurv-NET 和 RSV-NET 住院率。我们将基于近期住院情况和季节性的预测与使用老年人急诊科 (ED) 百分比、全年龄实验室阳性率或国家加权流感样疾病 (wILI) 的预测进行了比较。使用平均绝对误差 (MAE) 差异和 95% 置信区间 (CI) 在相同的预测周上评估准确性。其他比较使用相同的历史观察结果和替代季节性曲线。结果:在 120 个 RSV 预测周中,实验室阳性使 MAE 改善,每周每 100,000 人住院 0.096 例(95% CI 0.039-0.159)。单独的 ED 并没有明显改善预测(-0.059;-0.119 至 0.005),ED 也没有增加实验室阳性率。在 74 流感周,wILI 在主要季节性模型下将 MAE 提高了 0.266 (0.064-0.567)。使用相同的历史观察保留了这些主要发现。RSV 实验室收益在替代季节曲线下也持续存在,而使用更灵活的季节曲线的 wILI 估计值为 0.099(-0.062 至 0.299)。结论:在所检查的季节规格中,所有年龄段的实验室阳性率均改善了老年人 RSV 预测。一周流感 wILI 增量取决于季节性建模方式。ED 百分比没有提供一致的一周增量收益。

title: PREDICTORS OF NON-INVASIVE VENTILATION (NIV) FAILURE IN INFANTS AND CHILDREN WITH BRONCHIOLITIS
abstract: Background: Bronchiolitis is a major cause of hospitalization and critical care admission in infants and young children. Non-invasive ventilation (NIV) is increasingly used for respiratory support, but predictors of NIV failure in bronchiolitis remain incompletely defined. This study aimed to identify predictors of NIV failure in children younger than 2 years hospitalized with bronchiolitis. Methods: A bidirectional study was conducted at the Royal Hospital, Oman, over three bronchiolitis seasons from October 2023 to February 2026. Children younger than 2 years admitted to the pediatric intensive care unit or high-dependency unit with bronchiolitis requiring NIV were included. Demographic, clinical, radiological, virological, and physiological variables were collected. NIV failure was defined as the need for endotracheal intubation. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to identify independent predictors of NIV failure. Results: Of 330 children, 46 (13.9%) required intubation, while 284 (86.1%) were successfully managed with NIV. Independent predictors of NIV failure were RSV infection (aOR 2.75, 95% CI 1.25–6.06; P=0.012), radiographic lobar collapse (aOR 3.81, 95% CI 1.70–8.52; P=0.001), apnea (aOR 4.71, 95% CI 1.39–15.99; P=0.013), and higher pCO2 one hour after NIV initiation (aOR 1.05 per mmHg, 95% CI 1.01–1.10; P=0.010). Median time to intubation was 15 hours. Patients who failed NIV had a longer median critical care stay than those who succeeded (9.5 vs 5 days; P<0.001). Conclusion: NIV was successful in most children with bronchiolitis. RSV infection, lobar collapse, apnea, and higher pCO2 one hour after NIV initiation were independently associated with NIV failure. Early recognition of these predictors may help identify children requiring closer monitoring and timely escalation of respiratory support.

title: Immune checkpoint modulation beyond cancer: a conceptual framework for small-molecule host-directed antiviral therapy
abstract: Immune checkpoints are important regulators of antiviral immunity, but their roles in viral infections are more complex than the conventional model of immune inhibition. Although sustained checkpoint signaling can impair antiviral T-cell function and contribute to viral persistence, it can also limit immune-mediated tissue damage. This dual role presents a major challenge for therapeutic intervention, as indiscriminate checkpoint inhibition may improve viral control at the expense of increased immunopathology. In this review, we examine how viral infections reshape immune checkpoint networks through antiviral signaling, protein homeostasis, cellular metabolism, and tissue-specific immune regulation. We discuss the implications of these mechanisms for chronic viral infections, including human immunodeficiency virus and hepatitis B and C viruses, as well as acute respiratory infections caused by influenza A virus, severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2, and respiratory syncytial virus. Particular attention is given to small-molecule checkpoint modulators and their potential to regulate protein interactions, stability, localization, and signaling beyond conventional receptor–ligand blockade. We distinguish the pharmacological evidence supporting these compounds, which is derived primarily from oncology-related research, from the much more limited evidence of their direct antiviral activity. However, direct evidence that these compounds can achieve effective checkpoint modulation while improving viral control and limiting tissue injury remains limited. We therefore discuss the need for rigorous target validation and a more precise approach to patient selection and treatment design. Integrating viral burden, antiviral T-cell function, checkpoint activity, and inflammatory status may help identify patients most likely to benefit from intervention and guide treatment timing, intensity, and discontinuation. Combining checkpoint modulation with direct-acting antivirals or other host-directed therapies may offer additional benefits if viral suppression and immune restoration can be appropriately balanced. A shift from sustained checkpoint blockade toward context-dependent immune modulation may provide a basis for developing more precise host-directed antiviral strategies.

In this review, we examine how viral infections reshape immune checkpoint networks through antiviral signaling, protein homeostasis, cellular metabolism, and tissue-specific immune regulation. We discuss the implications of these mechanisms for chronic viral infections, including human immunodeficiency virus and hepatitis B and C viruses, as well as acute respiratory infections caused by influenza A virus, severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2, and respiratory syncytial virus. Particular attention is given to small-molecule checkpoint modulators and their potential to regulate protein interactions, stability, localization, and signaling beyond conventional receptor–ligand blockade. We distinguish the pharmacological evidence supporting these compounds, which is derived primarily from oncology-related research, from the much more limited evidence of their direct antiviral activity. However, direct evidence that these compounds can achieve effective checkpoint modulation while improving viral control and limiting tissue injury remains limited. We therefore discuss the need for rigorous target validation and a more precise approach to patient selection and treatment design. Integrating viral burden, antiviral T-cell function, checkpoint activity, and inflammatory status may help identify patients most likely to benefit from intervention and guide treatment timing, intensity, and discontinuation. Combining checkpoint modulation with direct-acting antivirals or other host-directed therapies may offer additional benefits if viral suppression and immune restoration can be appropriately balanced. A shift from sustained checkpoint blockade toward context-dependent immune modulation may provide a basis for developing more precise host-directed antiviral strategies.

abstract_zh: 免疫检查点是抗病毒药物免疫的重要调节因子,但其在病毒感染中的作用比传统的免疫抑制模型更为复杂。虽然持续的检查点信号传导会损害 抗病毒药物 T 细胞功能并导致病毒持续存在,但它也可以限制免疫介导的组织损伤。这种双重作用对治疗干预提出了重大挑战,因为不加区别的检查点抑制可能会以增强免疫病理学为代价来改善病毒控制。在这篇综述中,我们研究了病毒感染如何通过 抗病毒药物 信号传导、蛋白质稳态、细胞代谢和组织特异性免疫调节重塑免疫检查点网络。我们讨论这些机制对慢性病毒感染的影响,包括人类免疫缺陷病毒、乙型和丙型肝炎病毒,以及甲型流感病毒、严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2和呼吸道合胞病毒引起的急性呼吸道感染。特别关注小分子检查点调节剂及其调节蛋白质相互作用、稳定性、定位和信号传导超越传统受体-配体阻断的潜力。我们将支持这些化合物的药理学证据(主要来自肿瘤学相关研究)与其直接 抗病毒药物 活性的更为有限的证据区分开来。然而,表明这些化合物可以实现有效的检查点调节,同时改善病毒控制和限制组织损伤的直接证据仍然有限。因此,我们讨论了严格的目标验证以及更精确的患者选择和 治疗 设计方法的必要性。整合病毒负荷、抗病毒药物 T 细胞功能、检查点活性和炎症状态可能有助于识别最有可能从干预中受益的患者,并指导 治疗 的时机、强度和停药。如果病毒抑制和免疫恢复能够适当平衡,那么将检查点调节与直接作用的 抗病毒药物 或其他 宿主 定向疗法相结合可能会带来额外的好处。从持续的检查点封锁转向上下文相关的免疫调节可能为开发更精确的 宿主 导向的 抗病毒药物 策略提供基础。

title: The Relationship Between Upper Respiratory Tract Infections and the Incidence of Acute Otitis Media in Children: A Literature Review
abstract: Upper respiratory tract infection (URTI) is one of the most common illnesses in children and may lead to complications, one of which is acute otitis media (AOM). Children are more susceptible to AOM because their Eustachian tubes are relatively shorter and more horizontal, with immature drainage function. URTI can cause inflammation and edema of the nasopharynx, impairing Eustachian tube function and increasing the risk of AOM. This study was a literature review. A total of 10 journals published between 2021 and 2025 were reviewed and synthesized to determine the association between URTI and AOM in children, including relevant risk factors and pathogens. The review showed an association between URTI and AOM in children. (2025) reported a statistically significant association with a p-value of 0.019, while Azzahra et al. (2025) reported a p-value of 0.033 with a PR of 1.35. Several viruses, particularly respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and rhinovirus, were associated with AOM. Age, Eustachian tube anatomy, exposure to cigarette smoke, and air pollution may also increase the risk of AOM.URTI is associated with the occurrence of AOM in children through an inflammatory process that impairs Eustachian tube function and middle ear ventilation. Early detection of URTI, immunization, and control of environmental risk factors are needed to reduce the risk of AOM in children.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review investigates the relationship between upper respiratory tract infections (URTI) and the incidence of acute otitis media (AOM) in children, focusing on the role of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and rhinovirus as potential pathogens. The central question is whether URTI, particularly those caused by RSV and rhinovirus, increases the risk of AOM in children.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a literature analysis of 10 journals published between 2021 and 2025. It synthesizes findings to determine the association between URTI and AOM in children, including relevant risk factors and pathogens. The methodology involves reviewing and summarizing existing studies without conducting new experiments.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that URTI is associated with the occurrence of AOM in children through an inflammatory process that impairs Eustachian tube function and middle ear ventilation. It also identifies RSV and rhinovirus as particularly associated with AOM.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The evidence is limited to a literature review, and the findings are based on previously published studies. There is no mention of specific statistical methods or meta-analytic techniques used to consolidate the results. The review does not address the relative contributions of different pathogens or the mechanisms of inflammation in detail.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Early detection of URTI, immunization, and control of environmental risk factors are recommended to reduce the risk of AOM in children. Further research is needed to explore the specific roles of RSV and rhinovirus in AOM development and to identify effective interventions.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the link between upper respiratory tract infections (URTI) and acute otitis media (AOM) in children, emphasizing the role of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and rhinovirus. It highlights that URTI can lead to inflammation and edema in the nasopharynx, impairing Eustachian tube function and increasing AOM risk. The review synthesizes findings from 10 studies published between 2021 and 2025, concluding that URTI is associated with AOM through inflammatory processes. It also notes that RSV and rhinovirus are particularly linked to AOM. The review suggests early detection of URTI, immunization, and environmental risk factor control as strategies to reduce AOM incidence. However, it lacks detailed statistical methods and does not explore the mechanisms of inflammation further. Future research should focus on the specific roles of RSV and rhinovirus in AOM development and on effective interventions.

title_zh: 上呼吸道感染与儿童急性中耳炎发病率的关系文献综述
source_body_en: Upper respiratory tract infection (URTI) is one of the most common illnesses in children and may lead to complications, one of which is acute otitis media (AOM). Children are more susceptible to AOM because their Eustachian tubes are relatively shorter and more horizontal, with immature drainage function. URTI can cause inflammation and edema of the nasopharynx, impairing Eustachian tube function and increasing the risk of AOM. This study was a literature review. A total of 10 journals published between 2021 and 2025 were reviewed and synthesized to determine the association between URTI and AOM in children, including relevant risk factors and pathogens. The review showed an association between URTI and AOM in children. (2025) reported a statistically significant association with a p-value of 0.019, while Azzahra et al. (2025) reported a p-value of 0.033 with a PR of 1.35. Several viruses, particularly respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and rhinovirus, were associated with AOM. Age, Eustachian tube anatomy, exposure to cigarette smoke, and air pollution may also increase the risk of AOM.URTI is associated with the occurrence of AOM in children through an inflammatory process that impairs Eustachian tube function and middle ear ventilation. Early detection of URTI, immunization, and control of environmental risk factors are needed to reduce the risk of AOM in children.

title: Advancing Vaccine Adjuvants: Regulatory Frameworks and Developmental Strategies
abstract: Adjuvants have been an integral part of most vaccine formulations, mainly functioning as delivery systems and immunostimulants for antigens. Aluminum salts, the first adjuvants approved for human vaccine use, remain the most widely used adjuvants in EMA- and FDA-licensed vaccines. Adjuvants enhance vaccine-induced immune responses; improve vaccine efficacy, especially in populations vulnerable to infections such as the elderly and infants; provide antigen dose-sparing; and shape the immune profile of the vaccine-induced response. The effectiveness of vaccines is attributable primarily to the antigens as active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) and the adjuvants as constituent material in the vaccine formulation. Adjuvants enhance vaccine effectiveness by activating the innate immune system and boosting adaptive immune responses to co-delivered antigens. Adjuvants function as immunostimulants or delivery systems, often acting as both by promoting antigen uptake by Antigen Presenting Cells (APCs) and triggering cytokine and chemokine release to improve B and T cell activation. Adjuvants are either endogenous, as found in live, attenuated, pathogen-based vaccines, or exogenous, added to, e.g., protein subunit or mRNA-based vaccines to boost immunogenicity. Over the past few decades, novel exogenous adjuvants have become critical to new vaccine development, serving both as delivery systems and immune stimulants. Notable examples include MF59, used in seasonal and pandemic influenza vaccines, and AS01, incorporated in shingles, malaria, and RSV vaccines. The COVID-19 pandemic has accelerated not only the development and use of mRNA vaccines adjuvanted by lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) but also the development of novel adjuvants (e.g., Matrix M) and mimics (e.g., Advax-CpG) of those already present in licensed vaccines. While the growing interest in novel adjuvants has created new opportunities for development of vaccines and delivery systems, it has also introduced challenges in their development, regulation, and clinical application. The COVID-19 pandemic also exposed vulnerabilities in adjuvant availability and supply chains, underscoring the need for adjuvant mimics that can provide more accessible, scalable, and resilient alternatives. This paper explores the regulatory landscape surrounding the use of adjuvants in vaccines, highlighting critical aspects, opportunities and potential strategies for the development of novel adjuvants. It also addresses approaches to mitigate possible safety concerns and discusses the use of an adjuvant library established by the Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations (CEPI).

title_zh: 推进 疫苗 佐剂:监管框架和发展策略
source_body_en: Adjuvants have been an integral part of most vaccine formulations, mainly functioning as delivery systems and immunostimulants for antigens. Aluminum salts, the first adjuvants approved for human vaccine use, remain the most widely used adjuvants in EMA- and FDA-licensed vaccines. Adjuvants enhance vaccine-induced immune responses; improve vaccine efficacy, especially in populations vulnerable to infections such as the elderly and infants; provide antigen dose-sparing; and shape the immune profile of the vaccine-induced response. The effectiveness of vaccines is attributable primarily to the antigens as active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) and the adjuvants as constituent material in the vaccine formulation. Adjuvants enhance vaccine effectiveness by activating the innate immune system and boosting adaptive immune responses to co-delivered antigens. Adjuvants function as immunostimulants or delivery systems, often acting as both by promoting antigen uptake by Antigen Presenting Cells (APCs) and triggering cytokine and chemokine release to improve B and T cell activation. Adjuvants are either endogenous, as found in live, attenuated, pathogen-based vaccines, or exogenous, added to, e.g., protein subunit or mRNA-based vaccines to boost immunogenicity. Over the past few decades, novel exogenous adjuvants have become critical to new vaccine development, serving both as delivery systems and immune stimulants. Notable examples include MF59, used in seasonal and pandemic influenza vaccines, and AS01, incorporated in shingles, malaria, and RSV vaccines. The COVID-19 pandemic has accelerated not only the development and use of mRNA vaccines adjuvanted by lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) but also the development of novel adjuvants (e.g., Matrix M) and mimics (e.g., Advax-CpG) of those already present in licensed vaccines. While the growing interest in novel adjuvants has created new opportunities for development of vaccines and delivery systems, it has also introduced challenges in their development, regulation, and clinical application. The COVID-19 pandemic also exposed vulnerabilities in adjuvant availability and supply chains, underscoring the need for adjuvant mimics that can provide more accessible, scalable, and resilient alternatives. This paper explores the regulatory landscape surrounding the use of adjuvants in vaccines, highlighting critical aspects, opportunities and potential strategies for the development of novel adjuvants. It also addresses approaches to mitigate possible safety concerns and discusses the use of an adjuvant library established by the Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations (CEPI).
abstract_zh: 佐剂是大多数 疫苗 制剂的组成部分,主要用作抗原的递送系统和免疫刺激剂。铝盐是第一个被批准用于人类 疫苗 的佐剂,目前仍然是 EMA 和 FDA 许可的 疫苗 中使用最广泛的佐剂。佐剂增强疫苗诱导的免疫应答;提高疫苗的疗效,特别是在老年人和婴儿等易感染人群中;提供抗原剂量节约;并塑造 疫苗 诱导反应的免疫特征。疫苗 的有效性主要归因于作为活性药物成分(API)的抗原和作为 疫苗 制剂中的组成材料的佐剂。佐剂通过激活先天免疫系统并增强 免疫应答 对共递送抗原的适应性来增强 疫苗 的有效性。佐剂充当免疫刺激剂或递送系统,通常通过促进抗原呈递细胞 (APC) 摄取抗原并触发细胞因子和趋化因子释放来改善 B 和 T 细胞活化。佐剂可以是内源性的,如在活的、减毒的、基于病原体的疫苗中发现的,也可以是外源的,添加到例如蛋白质亚基或基于mRNA的疫苗中以增强免疫原性。在过去的几十年里,新型外源佐剂已成为新 疫苗 开发的关键,既可作为递送系统,又可作为免疫刺激剂。值得注意的例子包括用于季节性和大流行性流感 疫苗 的 MF59,以及用于带状疱疹、疟疾和 RSV 疫苗 的 AS01。COVID-19大流行不仅加速了脂质纳米粒子(LNP)佐剂的mRNA 疫苗的开发和使用,而且加速了已授权疫苗中已存在的新型佐剂(例如Matrix M)和模拟物(例如Advax-CpG)的开发。虽然人们对新型佐剂的兴趣日益浓厚,为 疫苗 和递送系统的开发创造了新的机遇,但也给它们的开发、监管和临床应用带来了挑战。COVID-19 大流行还暴露了佐剂供应和供应链的脆弱性,强调需要能够提供更容易获得、可扩展和有弹性的替代品的佐剂模拟物。本文探讨了 疫苗 中佐剂使用的监管环境,重点介绍了新型佐剂开发的关键方面、机遇和潜在策略。它还讨论了减轻可能的安全问题的方法,并讨论了流行病防范创新联盟 (CEPI) 建立的佐剂库的使用。

title: Risk of respiratory infections in closed communities: multi-dimensional risk assessment and integrated surveillance in a nursing home and a prison (Stell-ARI project)
abstract: Viral Acute Respiratory Infections (ARIs) are particularly relevant for people living in closed and vulnerable communities. The Stell-ARI Project aimed to design and apply a multi-dimensional framework integrating environmental risk assessment (based on building structure and management, resident population characteristics, indoor air quality (IAQ), and microbiological contamination of air and surfaces) with wastewater-based and clinical surveillance for SARS-CoV-2, Human Adenovirus (HAdV), Influenza Virus A (IVA) and B (IVB), Respiratory Syncytial Virus A (RSVA) and B (RSVB). This system was applied in two pilot institutional communities: a nursing home and a prison. The study design included questionnaire surveys of facility managers, residents and workers alongside environmental monitoring of chemical and microbial contaminants. Domain-specific and global risk scores were calculated. Scores were lower in the nursing home than in the prison for building structure and management (3 vs. 13) and resident population characteristics (3.4 vs. The chemical air risk score showed similar differences (1.3 vs. 3.0) and the two settings also differed in their indoor pollutant profiles. The microbiological air and surface risk score was also better in nursing home (4.0 vs 5.0). In both settings, a COVID-19 cluster was detected and SARS-CoV-2 and HAdV were found in air and surface samples, as well as in wastewater, not only in coincidence with clinical cases, but throughout the monitoring period, with a higher frequency in nursing home. In conclusion, this novel multi-dimensional structured approach, although needing further validation, represents a potential operational tool to support ARIs surveillance, prevention and control in closed and vulnerable institutional communities.

title_zh: 封闭社区呼吸道感染风险:疗养院和监狱的多维度风险评估和综合监测(Stell-ARI项目)

Domain-specific and global risk scores were calculated. Scores were lower in the nursing home than in the prison for building structure and management (3 vs. 13) and resident population characteristics (3.4 vs. The chemical air risk score showed similar differences (1.3 vs. 3.0) and the two settings also differed in their indoor pollutant profiles. In both settings, a COVID-19 cluster was detected and SARS-CoV-2 and HAdV were found in air and surface samples, as well as in wastewater, not only in coincidence with clinical cases, but throughout the monitoring period, with a higher frequency in nursing home. abstract_zh: 病毒性急性呼吸道感染(ARI)与生活在封闭和脆弱社区的人们尤其相关。Stell-ARI项目旨在设计和应用一个多维框架,将环境风险评估(基于建筑结构和管理、居民人口特征、室内空气质量(IAQ)以及空气和表面的微生物污染)与基于废水和临床的监测结合起来,用于SARS-CoV-2、人类腺病毒(HAdV)、流感病毒A(IVA)和B(IVB)、呼吸道合胞病毒 A(RSVA)和B (RSVB)。该系统在两个试点机构社区得到应用:疗养院和监狱。研究设计包括对设施管理人员、居民和工人进行问卷调查,以及对化学和微生物污染物的环境监测。计算了特定领域和全局风险评分。疗养院的建筑结构和管理(3 vs. 13)和居民人口特征(3.4 vs. 3.4 vs.)的得分均低于监狱。化学空气风险评分显示出相似的差异(1.3 vs. 3.0),两种环境的室内污染物特征也存在差异。疗养院的微生物空气和表面风险评分也更好(4.0 vs 5.0)。在这两种环境中,均检测到了 COVID-19 簇以及 SARS-CoV-2 和 HAdV在空气和地表样本以及废水中都发现了这种病毒,不仅与临床病例相符,而且在整个监测期间,在疗养院中出现的频率更高。总之,这种新颖的多维结构化方法虽然需要进一步验证,但却是支持 ARIs 监测、封闭和脆弱机构社区预防和控制的潜在操作工具。

title: Quantitative Microbial Risk Assessment of Airborne Viruses and Semi-Quantitative Bacterial Risk Scoring in Occupied European Indoor Environments: A Multi-Country Study
abstract: Quantitative microbial risk assessment (QMRA) is well established for waterborne and foodborne hazards but rarely applied to airborne pathogens in real occupied buildings, where viral loads are low, intermittent, and left-censored and where bacterial monitoring yields only presence/absence data. We applied a dual bioaerosol framework—probabilistic single-hit dose–response modelling for respiratory viruses and a transparent semi-quantitative scoring model for bacteria—across twenty-two micro-environments in six European countries. Air was sampled with a Sartorius MD8 Airport sampler and gelatin membrane filters on one to four days per phase, and SARS-CoV-2, adenovirus, influenza A, RSV, and rhinovirus were quantified by RT-qPCR, with influenza B assayed but never detected (method limits of detection 437–1860 copies m−3). Exposure was expressed in genome copies, the unit measured, and each dose–response parameter was re-expressed per genome copy, so that the conversion between genome copies and infectious units is carried explicitly by the parameter and propagated as a distribution. Airborne material was subject to first-order inactivation at a rate determined by the measured temperature and relative humidity, which were resampled in pairs from the room’s own sensor record where one covered the sampling days (100,000 Monte Carlo iterations). In the twelve micro-environments with a usable environmental record, the resulting upper-bound probability of infection per occupant per day—for one occupant present through one occupied day on which the agent was detected, infection rather than illness being the endpoint of every parameter used—ranged from 9.0 × 10−7 for influenza A to 0.9998 for SARS-CoV-2 and 0.97 for adenovirus in the most contaminated rooms. These bounds approach their upper limit of 1 and, therefore, stop distinguishing between rooms, and we report them as a measurement of the exposure metric rather than as a forecast: at concentrations reaching 8.4 × 106 genome copies m−3, a genome-copy dose exceeds the published per-infection dose by one to three orders of magnitude, so absolute risk cannot be recovered without knowing the infectious fraction, which RT-qPCR does not measure. Concentrations of a given agent spanned a median factor of five, and up to 283-fold, between the lowest and highest positive sample of a room–phase series, and up to 471-fold between two sampled days anywhere in the network. In a random-effects decomposition of log10 concentration the within-series standard deviation exceeds the between-series one for both agents modelled on repeated samples (0.58 against 0.37 for SARS-CoV-2, 0.49 against 0.22 for adenovirus), so that most of the variation is between days within a room rather than between rooms and a single sampling event characterises neither. That comparison, like the comparison between phases, is made on measured concentrations and is, therefore, unaffected by the unknown scaling. Measured airborne viral concentrations did not fall systematically after the installation of portable air cleaners, and changed in the same direction in rooms that received no device, so no effect can be attributed to the intervention in this design. Swab-derived bacterial scores fell in four of the six micro-environments with paired data, by 32% to 54%, and the air samples yielded more bacterial species than occupant swabs on three of the six occasions on which the two matrices can be compared, substantially so on two of them. For three of the four agents modelled, the dominant uncertainty is the number of genome copies per infectious unit, to which the inhaled dose is proportional and the estimates are proportional until the bound approaches one; for SARS-CoV-2 it is the published range of the genome-copy dose–response parameter, which spans a factor of fifteen. The absolute values are, therefore, upper bounds for SARS-CoV-2, adenovirus, and rhinovirus, while the influenza A values rest on a parameter fitted to attenuated strains and understate the risk from wild-type virus. The conclusions rest on the relative comparisons.

In a random-effects decomposition of log10 concentration the within-series standard deviation exceeds the between-series one for both agents modelled on repeated samples (0.58 against 0.37 for SARS-CoV-2, 0.49 against 0.22 for adenovirus), so that most of the variation is between days within a room rather than between rooms and a single sampling event characterises neither. That comparison, like the comparison between phases, is made on measured concentrations and is, therefore, unaffected by the unknown scaling. Measured airborne viral concentrations did not fall systematically after the installation of portable air cleaners, and changed in the same direction in rooms that received no device, so no effect can be attributed to the intervention in this design. Swab-derived bacterial scores fell in four of the six micro-environments with paired data, by 32% to 54%, and the air samples yielded more bacterial species than occupant swabs on three of the six occasions on which the two matrices can be compared, substantially so on two of them. For three of the four agents modelled, the dominant uncertainty is the number of genome copies per infectious unit, to which the inhaled dose is proportional and the estimates are proportional until the bound approaches one; for SARS-CoV-2 it is the published range of the genome-copy dose–response parameter, which spans a factor of fifteen. The absolute values are, therefore, upper bounds for SARS-CoV-2, adenovirus, and rhinovirus, while the influenza A values rest on a parameter fitted to attenuated strains and understate the risk from wild-type virus. The conclusions rest on the relative comparisons.

title: Double trouble: combined exposures of airway epithelial cells to air pollutants and respiratory viruses
abstract: Air pollution and respiratory viral infections are major contributors to the global burden of respiratory disease. Epidemiological studies suggest that air pollution increases the severity of viral infections, yet the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. This dissertation presents research on how combined exposure to air pollutants and respiratory pathogens affects airway epithelial responses, using human in vitro models. First, combined exposure to particulate matter, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and Streptococcus pneumoniae revealed that RSV predominantly drives epithelial inflammatory responses, which can be further enhanced by particulate matter. Next, a continuous exposure system was developed to investigate interactions between nitrogen dioxide (NO2) and RSV infection over prolonged periods. Using this system, concurrent NO2 exposure unexpectedly reduced RSV viral load and associated pro-inflammatory cytokine responses, contrasting with epidemiological observations. Further mechanistic investigations demonstrated that NO2 modulates the membrane expression of RSV entry-related proteins, nucleolin and insulin-like growth factor 1 receptor, depending on the time point after exposure. Together, these findings demonstrate that air pollutants can modify epithelial responses to respiratory pathogens, highlighting the complexity of exposure interactions. They also underline the importance of exposure timing relative to infection and provides a foundation for future mechanistic research linking air pollution to respiratory disease severity.

title: Metabolic reprogramming and immune-metabolic interactions in Respiratory viral infections
abstract: Respiratory viruses, including influenza, RSV, and SARS-CoV-2, hijack host metabolic machinery to facilitate their replication and evade immune surveillance. This review synthesizes current evidence on the bidirectional interplay between viral-induced metabolic reprogramming – specifically the upregulation of glycolysis, lipogenesis, and glutaminolysis, and the disruption of mitochondrial homeostasis – and the host immune response. We highlight how this metabolic rewiring not only provides biosynthetic precursors for viral proliferation but also modulates immune cell differentiation and inflammatory outcomes. Furthermore, we discuss how preexisting host metabolic conditions (e.g. obesity, diabetes, aging) exacerbate disease severity through this metabolic-immune axis, and how persistent metabolic alterations may underlie post-acute sequelae such as Long COVID. Finally, we evaluate the therapeutic potential and challenges of targeting metabolic checkpoints, such as mTOR and SREBP, to balance antiviral efficacy with immune homeostasis. PubMed was searched for articles from database inception to July 2026.

full_text: Abstract Background COVID-19 non-pharmaceutical interventions (NPIs) altered disrupted respiratory pathogen transmission, but the medium-term epidemiological evolution of Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and any co-detection patterns after NPI relaxation remains unclear. This multicenter study (2019–2025) comprehensively characterized RSV dynamics and mixed infections with Human rhinovirus (HRV), Mycoplasma pneumoniae (MP), and human adenovirus (HAdV) across four pandemic phases, aiming to identify post-pandemic changes. Methods A total of 108,701 hospitalized children in Fujian were enrolled, each contributing one respiratory specimen for multiplex PCR testing. We compared RSV positivity, seasonality, age distribution, and co-detection patterns (RSV + HRV, RSV + MP, RSV+HAdV) across four phases: pre-pandemic (Phase 1), strict NPI (Phase 2), policy transition (Phase 3), and post-pandemic (Phase 4). Results Overall RSV positivity was 12.37% (13,241/107,015). RSV declined during the strict NPI phase (9.41%) compared with the pre-pandemic phase (17.12%), reached its lowest level during the policy transition phase (5.72%), and rebounded in the post-pandemic phase (13.62%). The traditional winter peak shifted to autumn ((22.32%) and summer (16.08%). Infants < 1 year remained highest-risk (22.30%), yet post-pandemic co-infections shifted toward 3–6-year-olds (39.53% of mixed infections children). MP showed extreme suppression (0.32%) and marked rebound (32.61% in winter), while HRV remained stable and HAdV showed an intermediate response. The RSV co-detection rate per child tested was 1.76% pre-pandemic, 0.83% during the NPI period, and 2.12% post-pandemic, representing a 2.55-fold increase over the NPI period (95% CI: 2.24–2.90) and a 1.20-fold increase over pre-pandemic levels (95% CI: 0.95–1.53); RSV + HRV dominated (76.55%), but RSV + MP recovered dramatically (11.26% vs. 1.82% during mitigation). Importantly, this study provides long-term evidence from subtropical China that NPIs suppressed RSV and that the resulting seasonal displacement—with the winter peak replaced by summer–autumn predominance—has persisted for approximately three seasons and has not yet reverted. Moreover, the post-pandemic age expansion—with co-infections in children < 3 years dropping below 50% for the first time—may reflect, among other mechanisms, an immunity debt in older preschool children; however, our dataset cannot directly measure immunity, and this hypothesis requires confirmation with serological and birth-cohort data. Conclusions COVID-19 mitigation measures may have altered altered RSV’s seasonality, age distribution, and co-detection patterns. Among the pathogens examined, MP exhibited the largest changes in positivity across phases. Ongoing surveillance and age-stratified prevention strategies are urgently needed to address the re-emerging burden of RSV and its mixed infections. analysis.summary_en: This study analyzed the epidemiological characteristics and changing transmission patterns of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) among hospitalized children with acute respiratory tract infections (ARTIs) in Fujian Province, China, from 2019 to 2025. It compared RSV positivity, seasonality, age distribution, and co-detection patterns with other pathogens across four pandemic phases: pre-pandemic, strict NPI, policy transition, and post-pandemic. The results showed a decline in RSV positivity during the strict NPI phase, reaching its lowest level during the policy transition phase, followed by a rebound in the post-pandemic phase. The traditional winter peak shifted to autumn and summer, and co-infections shifted toward older children. The authors suggest that these changes may reflect an immunity debt in preschoolers, though this requires further confirmation. The study emphasizes the need for ongoing surveillance and age-specific prevention strategies to manage the re-emerging RSV burden. The evidence is moderate due to the retrospective design and lack of direct immunity measurements.

full_text: Abstract Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a major cause of lower respiratory tract infections worldwide, particularly in infants, older adults, and immunocompromised individuals. The development of peptide-based antivirals represents a promising strategy to complement existing preventive and therapeutic approaches. In this study, a computational peptide engineering workflow was employed to design mastoparan-derived peptides targeting RSV structural proteins. A library of 60 mastoparan-derived peptide variants was generated in silico using custom Python scripts in a Linux (Ubuntu) environment through systematic point mutations, sequence hybridization, and de novo design rules while preserving key physicochemical properties. Following multi-parameter screening based on physicochemical descriptors, structural stability, and predicted biological activity, 39 candidates were selected for further analysis. PM2 was identified as a top-ranked candidate and was subsequently modified through a targeted point mutation to generate a novel derivative peptide. The three-dimensional structure of the mutated peptide was predicted using AlphaFold, and its interaction with the RSV fusion protein (RSV F) was evaluated using HADDOCK molecular docking. The RSV F-MutantPM2 complex was evaluated by a 100 ns Molecular Dynamics simulation. The complex reached equilibrium after approximately 20 ns and remained stable throughout the simulation, with a mean backbone RMSD of 0.32 nm. The Radius of Gyration remained stable at 3.06 nm, indicating preserved structural compactness. A persistent intermolecular hydrogen-bonding network was observed, averaging 9.18 hydrogen bonds. RMSF analysis showed low flexibility at the RSV F binding interface (0.18 nm), while MutantPM2 exhibited moderate flexibility (0.42 nm), indicating adaptive peptide dynamics within a stable binding pocket and sustained complex association and MutantPM2 forms stable dynamic interactions with prefusion antigenic Site IV (residues 422–438) within the F1 subdomain (residues 390–496). These findings establish a compelling, testable structural hypothesis for targeted prefusion stabilization and potential interference with the fusion cascade, providing a clear structural roadmap for subsequent experimental validation, that demonstrating a preferential predicted binding propensity toward RSV F over other viral structural proteins (G and M). Overall, this study presents an iterative in silico peptide engineering approach integrating sequence design, structure prediction, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations to prioritize peptide candidates with potential antiviral activity against RSV. Among the candidates evaluated, MutantPM2 emerged as a promising candidate for subsequent experimental validation and biophysical characterization. analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: PM2 was identified as a top-ranked candidate and was subsequently modified through a targeted point mutation to generate a novel derivative peptide. analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to develop peptide-based antivirals against respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) by employing a computational peptide engineering workflow. A library of 60 mastoparan-derived peptides was generated in silico through systematic mutations and hybridization, with 39 selected for further analysis. The top candidate, PM2, was modified to create MutantPM2, and its interaction with RSV fusion protein (RSV F) was evaluated using AlphaFold and HADDOCK. Molecular dynamics simulations showed that the RSV F-MutantPM2 complex reached equilibrium and remained stable, with a mean backbone RMSD of 0.32 nm and a persistent hydrogen-bonding network. MutantPM2 exhibited stable dynamic interactions with prefusion antigenic Site IV of RSV F, suggesting a potential antiviral mechanism. The findings provide a structural hypothesis for targeted prefusion stabilization and may guide future experimental validation. However, the study is limited to computational methods, and the evidence is moderate in strength due to the absence of experimental confirmation.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 是全世界下呼吸道感染的主要原因,特别是在婴儿、老年人和免疫功能低下的个体中。基于肽的 抗病毒药物 的开发代表了一种有前途的策略,可以补充现有的预防和治疗方法。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 采用计算肽工程工作流程来设计针对 RSV 结构蛋白的乳腺衍生肽。在 Linux (Ubuntu) 环境中使用自定义 Python 脚本,通过系统点 突变、序列杂交和从头设计规则,在计算机上生成了 60 个乳腺衍生肽变体的库,同时保留了关键的理化特性。根据理化描述符、结构稳定性和预测的生物活性进行多参数筛选后,选择了 39 名候选者进行进一步分析。
elements_zh.methods: 使用AlphaFold预测突变肽的三维结构,并使用HADDOCK分子对接评估其与RSV融合蛋白(RSV F)的相互作用。通过 100 ns 分子动力学模拟评估 RSV F-MutantPM2 复合物。
elements_zh.main_results: 该复合物在大约 20 ns 后达到平衡,并在整个模拟过程中保持稳定,平均主链 RMSD 为 0.32 nm。回转半径保持稳定在 3.06 nm,表明结构紧凑。观察到持久的分子间氢键网络,平均 9.18 个氢键。RMSF 分析显示 RSV F 结合界面的灵活性较低(0.18 nm),而 MutantPM2 表现出中等灵活性(0.42 nm),表明稳定结合袋内的适应性肽动力学和持续的复合物关联,并且 MutantPM2 与 F1 子域(残基 390-496)内的融合前抗原位点 IV(残基 422-438)形成稳定的动态相互作用。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: PM2 被确定为排名靠前的候选者,随后通过靶向点 突变 进行修饰,生成新型衍生肽。这些发现为靶向预融合稳定和融合级联的潜在干扰建立了令人信服的、可测试的结构假设,为后续实验验证提供了清晰的结构路线图,证明了与其他病毒结构蛋白(G和M)相比,对RSV F的优先预测结合倾向。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 本研究提出了一种迭代的计算机肽工程方法,集成了序列设计、结构预测、分子对接和分子动力学模拟,以优先考虑具有潜在 抗病毒药物 抗 RSV 活性的候选肽。这些发现为后续实验验证提供了清晰的结构路线图,并可能为针对 RSV 的新型 抗病毒药物 策略的开发提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于计算机分析,不包括实验验证。证据基于计算模型和模拟,可能无法完全反映生物学现实。由于依赖未经实验证实的预测计算方法,置信度中等。
